m-ff7eff55.t: Estonia's Tax and Customs Board states (page updated 16 September 2026) that from April 2027 VAT payers submit the transaction data behind the VAT return, not the return form, from accounting software or e-MTA; the intra-Community supply report joins the return; invoices under EUR 1,000 and those to private persons 'still need not be declared'. The enacted rewrite of VAT Act § 27 is dated 1 January 2027; the page leaves the three-month gap unexplained. The Board ties mandatory e-invoices to the EU VAT change applying from 1 July 2030; no Estonian act sets a general e-invoice duty earlier as of 5 October 2026, but a registered e-invoice recipient may demand one (Accounting Act § 7^1).

m-fe4735a5.t: Form TSD is set by Minister of Finance Regulation No 60 of 29 November 2010. Until 4 October 2026 it had a main form and eight annexes: 1 payments to resident natural persons; 2 payments to non-residents; 3 profit taken out of a non-resident's permanent establishment; 4 fringe benefits; 5 gifts, donations, entertainment expenses; 6 non-business expenses, taxation-mismatch amounts; 7 dividends, equity payouts, hidden distributions, CFC profit, exit tax; 8 international sea carriage (3 and 7 also: banks' advance tax). In the text in force from 5 October 2026 (RT I, 02.10.2026, 16) Annex 1 is the 'Payments made to persons' part of form TSD, Annex 2 is repealed; Annexes 3-8 and form INF 1 stay.

m-fcbb0505.t: Banks are the exception to Estonia's rule of taxing profit only on distribution. Under Income Tax Act § 47^1 a resident credit institution and the Estonian branch of a non-resident one pay an advance income tax by the 10th day of the third month of each quarter on the previous quarter's profit. The rate (§ 4(5)) was 14% from 1 January 2018 to 31 December 2024 and is 18% from 1 January 2025 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107), in force on 5 October 2026. A draft Riigikogu resolution (1038 OE, introduced by the Centre Party group on 29 September 2026) proposes that the Government change the taxation of bank profits; it is a proposal to the Government, not a bill, and is not adopted.

m-f95e7b2b.t: Estonia taxes a loan to a shareholder as a hidden profit distribution where the facts point that way. Under Income Tax Act § 50^2 (in force since 1 January 2018, act published RT I, 07.07.2017, 3) a resident company pays income tax on a loan given to its shareholder, partner or member 'if the circumstances of the transaction indicate that it may be a hidden profit distribution'. For a loan to a parent company or to a fellow subsidiary (other than the lender's own subsidiary) with a repayment term longer than 48 months, the taxpayer must, at the tax authority's request, prove the ability and intention to repay, with at least 30 days to produce evidence. In force 5 October 2026.

m-f6d3b47c.t: The OECD Multilateral Instrument did not change the company tie-breaker of the Estonia–Cyprus tax convention. The synthesised text prepared jointly by the two competent authorities (Estonia's Ministry of Finance, late 2021) inserts only three MLI provisions — Art. 6(1) (preamble), the first sentence of Art. 16(1) (mutual agreement procedure) and Art. 7(1) (principal purposes test) — and reproduces Art. 4(3) unchanged. Per its footnotes these apply for taxes withheld at source from 1 January 2022 in both states, and for other taxes for taxable periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 in Estonia and 25 June 2022 in Cyprus; the Ministry's table shows only 'MLI effective from 01.01.2022'.

m-f36ad55c.t: The Estonian Tax and Customs Board's e-services environment e-MTA accepts login with other EEA states' eIDs: its page for foreigners (last updated 19 February 2026) says a foreigner can enter with 'the European Union digital identity card (eID)', an Estonian ID-card (including an e-resident's digital ID) or Estonian Mobile-ID or Smart-ID, and its list of eID tools 'with a high assurance level' names 23 states, among them 'Cyprus — Cyprus National eID — IDMe.cy'. On first entry by 'EU eID' a user account is created and customer support then opens the e-services; a legal representative needing access on behalf of a company must ask the Board separately.

m-ef552edb.t: Estonia has no annual corporate income tax return. The Tax and Customs Board states: 'Estonia does not have a corporate tax return covering the taxable income of the entire calendar year'; a company declares income tax, social tax, funded pension contributions and unemployment insurance premiums on the monthly form TSD, and where it made no taxable payments in a month and has no information to submit 'there is no need to file TSD tax returns containing only zeros'. A TSD is still due without tax where, for example, a taxable payment yields zero tax or a contribution to equity is paid in (Annex 7). A VAT-registered company, by contrast, files a VAT return even with no supply in the period.

m-edb0455c.t: Fees an Estonian OÜ pays its board member are taxed in Estonia even when the member lives abroad (Estonian texts in force on 5 October 2026). Income Tax Act § 29(2) taxes income a non-resident receives for performing the duties of a member of the management or controlling body of a resident legal person; the company withholds the tax (§ 41 point 2) at the § 4(1) rate, 22% (§ 43(1) point 1), final for the non-resident (§ 43(4)) unless a tax treaty sets a lower rate (§ 43(2)). Social Tax Act § 2(1) point 4 puts social tax on such fees, at 33% (§ 7(1)); per the Tax and Customs Board it is not due only if the recipient holds an A1 certificate of social security coverage from his home country.

m-ed317056.t: A natural person is an Estonian tax resident if his or her place of residence is in Estonia or if he or she stays in Estonia for at least 183 days in a period of 12 consecutive calendar months; the person counts as resident from the day of arrival (Income Tax Act § 6(1)). A resident is taxed on worldwide income, a non-resident only on the Estonian-source income listed in § 29 (§ 6(1), (3)). The person must tell the tax authority of circumstances that change residence and fill in the residence form (form R) (§ 6(6)); a treaty tie-breaker prevails over the statutory test (§ 6(5)). e-Residency is a digital identity and is not among the tests. In force 5 October 2026.

m-e862ab1f.t: Estonia has no unconditional duty to issue e-invoices between businesses as of 5 October 2026, but a buyer can impose one. Accounting Act § 7(5) says a source document must be machine-processable, yet allows another written form where a party cannot handle such documents without disproportionate cost. Under § 7^1(3) and (7), in force since 1 July 2025 (act RT I, 10.10.2024, 1), an accounting entity that wants only machine-processable invoices is marked in the commercial register as an e-invoice recipient and may then require the seller to present one; an e-invoice meeting standard EN 16931-1 is presumed proper; parties may agree another standard. The text enacted for 2027 keeps § 7^1.

m-e846bc8a.t: Art. 15 of the Estonia–Cyprus tax convention (Directors' fees) lets the company's state tax a board member resident in the other state: 'Directors' fees and other similar payments derived by a resident of a Contracting State in his capacity as a member of the board of directors or any other similar organ of a company which is a resident of the other Contracting State may be taxed in that other State.' So Estonia's domestic rule taxing a non-resident board member's fee from an Estonian company (Income Tax Act § 29(2)) is not switched off by the treaty for a Cyprus resident; 'may be taxed' does not make the taxation exclusive.

m-e632db8e.t: Estonian tax acts do not oblige a café to run a cash register, but the Alcohol Act does once it sells alcohol (texts in force on 5 October 2026). Value-Added Tax Act § 37(3): an invoice meeting § 37 need not be issued for a supply to a natural person for personal use (three listed cases excepted). The Value-Added Tax, Income Tax and Consumer Protection Acts do not mention a cash register. Alcohol Act § 44 permits retail sale of alcoholic drinks in a shop or catering establishment only where a cash register is on the premises and records every such sale; Taxation Act § 70(1) point 4 and (2) lets the tax authority demand installation where a law obliges it.

m-e5737d1a.t: A sole proprietor (FIE) in Estonia pays income tax at 22% on business income after deductible expenses and social tax at 33% on the same net income, the latter with a floor and a cap: at least twelve times the monthly rate a year (EUR 886 a month in 2026) and at most ten times the sum of the monthly minimum wages of the year (Social Tax Act § 2(1) point 5, § 2(5)). Social tax is paid in quarterly advances by the 15th day of the third month of each quarter, each equal to three monthly rates x 33%, with the balance due by 1 October of the following year (§ 9(3)). A sole proprietor is not covered by unemployment insurance. In force 5 October 2026.

m-e56f0e1a.t: From 2018 to 2024 Estonia taxed regular dividends at a lower corporate rate: the part of a calendar year's distributed profit not exceeding the average of the previous three calendar years' taxed distributions bore 14% with divisor 0.86 (14/86) (Income Tax Act § 4(5) and § 50^1, in force 1 January 2018, act RT I, 07.07.2017, 3). 2018 was the first year counted, so the rate first applied in 2019, to one third of the profit distributed in 2018 (§ 61(53)). On such a dividend paid to a natural person, resident or non-resident, the company withheld a further 7% (§ 4(4), § 18(1^3), § 29(7^1), § 41 point 7^2). The act of 20 June 2023 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107) repealed these rules from 1 January 2025.

m-dd351274.t: Personal income tax in Estonia is a flat 22% in 2026 (20% from 2015 to 2024; 22% from 1 January 2025), with 10% on certain pension and insurance payouts (Income Tax Act § 4(1)-(2)). A resident natural person files a return for the year by 30 April of the next year, unless income did not exceed the basic exemption or no further tax is due (§ 44(6); sole proprietors and some others must still file, § 44(6^1)); the pre-filled return opens on 15 February (§ 44(1), (1^1)); tax assessed is due by 1 October (§ 46(3)). A non-resident files only for income from which tax was not withheld under § 41; withheld tax is final unless the income came through an Estonian permanent establishment (§ 43(4)).

m-da85b5b5.t: To declare a payment to a non-resident - on form TSD or, for dividend recipients, on form INF 1 - an Estonian company needs the recipient's Estonian code: a personal identification code, a registry code or, failing those, a non-resident code issued by the Tax and Customs Board. The recipient or the payer applies for it; the Board says it issues the code 'within 10 days'. An e-resident already has an Estonian personal identification code. The code does not open treaty rates: for those the Board must also hold a certificate of residence from the foreign tax authority (form TM3 or equivalent), valid 12 months for a natural person and 36 for a legal person. Read 5 October 2026.

m-d9767328.t: Cross-border VAT schemes in Estonia as of 5 October 2026: (1) a seller established only in Estonia may keep Estonian VAT on distance sales of goods and telecom and electronic services to consumers in other member states while these stay within EUR 10,000 in the previous and current year (Value-Added Tax Act § 10^1(7)-(9)); otherwise it may use the OSS scheme via e-MTA - quarterly, return and payment by the end of the next month (IOSS: monthly); (2) since 1 January 2025 an Estonian business with Union turnover up to EUR 100,000 may, after notifying the Estonian tax authority, use another member state's small-enterprise exemption within that state's threshold (§ 19^1), reporting quarterly.

m-d8bde8e8.t: An Estonian company does not apply separately to be registered as a taxpayer - a reading of § 18(1) of the Taxation Act as in force on 5 October 2026, not a sentence of it. It lists who must register with the Tax and Customs Board before starting activity in Estonia; of Estonian legal persons it names only one 'that is not entered in the commercial register, the register of non-profit associations and foundations or the register of religious associations' (p 1; the other points cover public agencies, non-residents and associations without legal personality). An OÜ, being in the commercial register, is thus outside the duty. VAT registration is a separate step under the Value-Added Tax Act.

m-ce02a0ba.t: The Estonian Tax and Customs Board's comparison of business forms (page last updated 14 May 2026, read 5 October 2026): an entrepreneur-account holder files no returns and cannot deduct expenses, and 'currently, entrepreneur accounts can only be opened at the LHV Pank'; a sole proprietor (FIE) reports once a year on income tax return form E, may deduct business expenses and pays advance social tax of EUR 877.14 per quarter in 2026; an OÜ files monthly returns (TSD, KMD, KMD INF) and an annual report to the Business Register. If receipts on an entrepreneur account exceed EUR 40,000 in a calendar year the person must register as a FIE or OÜ and for VAT.

m-caf023ea.t: Estonia transposed DAC7 (platform reporting) as chapter 2^4 of the Tax Information Exchange Act, in force since 1 January 2023 (act published RT I, 29.12.2022, 1). An Estonian-resident platform operator identifies reportable sellers by 31 December and reports them to the tax authority by 31 January of the next year; reportable activities are renting immovable property, time- or task-based services, sale of goods and renting means of transport. Among the sellers excluded (§ 20^22(3)): one with fewer than 30 sales of goods and at most EUR 2,000 of consideration in the year. Software that only enables payment processing, listing or advertising, or redirecting users is no platform (§ 20^20(2)).

m-c8e4ab00.t: A management board member's fee paid by an Estonian company bears income tax (22%, withheld) and social tax (33%, paid by the company) and, for a resident in the second pension pillar, the funded pension contribution, but no unemployment insurance premium: a board member outside the Employment Contracts Act is not insured. Social tax falls on the fee actually paid: the monthly minimum base of Social Tax Act § 2(2) names employees and officials, and the Tax and Customs Board's example of an e-resident board member on EUR 100 a month gives EUR 22 income tax, EUR 33 social tax, company cost EUR 133. Bases: Income Tax Act § 13(2), § 41; Social Tax Act § 2(1) p 4; Unemployment Insurance Act § 3.

m-c71fa158.t: Proposed, not adopted as of 5 October 2026: Government bill 992 SE 'Act amending the Value-Added Tax Act', introduced in the Riigikogu on 14 September 2026, first reading completed on 28 September 2026, amendments due by 12 October 2026. Per the Riigikogu's summary it transposes amendments of the EU VAT Directive and widens the use of the one-stop-shop (OSS) scheme so that a business can meet VAT obligations arising in other member states through its home state; the bill text cites Directive (EU) 2025/516. Proposed commencement: 1 January 2027, with a listed set of points on 1 July 2028. The bill text contains no change of VAT rates and no e-invoicing provision.

m-c6a0d640.t: No general duty to install a cash register was found in Estonia's Taxation Act on 5 October 2026: § 70(1) point 4 only lets the tax authority demand that a taxpayer install 'devices enabling the monitoring of cash settlements, including a cash register', and § 70(2) allows that demand where the taxpayer has not met a duty to install such a device imposed on it by law. One such duty exists for shops, cafes and restaurants selling alcohol: under § 44 of the Alcohol Act retail sale of alcoholic beverages in a shop or catering establishment is permitted only if the place of business has a cash register through which every retail sale of alcohol is recorded (in force since 15 April 2004).

m-c26327c3.t: Under Estonian domestic law a company's tax residence follows incorporation only: a legal person is resident 'if it is established under Estonian law', and so are a European company (SE) and a European cooperative (SCE) whose seat is registered in Estonia (Income Tax Act § 6(2)). The Act has no place-of-management test for legal persons; but § 6(5) gives way to a tax treaty where residence determined under the treaty differs from residence under the Act. Estonian text read, version in force 1 October – 31 December 2026 (RT I, 09.07.2026, 66).

m-c1fdec92.t: A person without an Estonian ID document can sign in to the Estonian Tax and Customs Board's e-MTA with another member state's eID, per the Board (page updated 20 February 2026, read 5 October 2026): its list of accepted schemes, limited to means 'with a high assurance level', includes for Cyprus the 'Cyprus National eID' (IDMe.cy). At first sign-in with 'EU eID' a user account is created, after which the person 'must then contact the customer support' to have e-services opened; a legal representative who needs access on behalf of a company asks for it by message in e-MTA or by e-mail. Mobile-ID and Smart-ID need an Estonian personal identification code.

m-c18bab93.t: The Estonia–Cyprus Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income, with its Protocol, was signed in Luxembourg on 15 October 2012 in English, entered into force on 8 October 2013 (Foreign Ministry notice, RT II, 15.10.2013, 4) and under its Art. 26(2) has effect from 1 January 2014. It was in force on 5 October 2026. Estonia's Ministry of Finance table (updated 7 April 2026) gives the same in-force and effective dates but shows the signing date as 15.10.2011, which conflicts with the treaty text and the notice.

m-c05f2556.t: The Tax and Customs Board's page on companies established by e-residents (read 5 October 2026) warns that 'e-residency in Estonia does not give an automatic exemption from foreign tax liabilities': if the e-resident manages the Estonian company from outside Estonia it 'will probably have a permanent establishment abroad' and income tax on that profit is due in the foreign state. Board members whose remuneration is taxable in Estonia must be entered by the company in the employment register, and the payments are declared in Annex 2 of form TSD by the 10th day of the month after payment. On a dividend the company pays 22/78 and nothing further is withheld from an e-resident natural person.

m-bd565018.t: Estonia transposed DAC8 (crypto-asset reporting, with other changes to administrative cooperation) by an act adopted on 25 March 2026, published RT I, 15.04.2026, 1 and in force from 25 April 2026, which added chapter 1^2 to the Tax Information Exchange Act. A reporting crypto-asset service provider applies the reporting and due diligence rules for the first time to collect information for 2026 and reports for the first time by 30 June 2027; for users who were clients on 31 December 2025 it must identify the reportable ones by 1 January 2027 (§ 23^8). The Tax and Customs Board lists DAC2/CRS/FATCA, DAC4, DAC6, DAC7 and DAC8/CARF as the tax information exchange returns it receives.

m-b99ecebe.t: A fee paid by an Estonian company to a board member who is not an Estonian resident is taxed in Estonia wherever the work is done. Income Tax Act § 29(2) taxes a non-resident's income for performing the duties of a member of the management or supervisory body of a resident legal person; § 41 point 2 makes the company withhold. The Tax and Customs Board's page for e-residents' companies (4 November 2025) says the company 'must pay income tax and social tax in Estonia regardless of the location where work is carried on', reports the fee on form TSD (the page names Annex 2, dropped from the form in October 2026) and registers a member with a fee taxable in Estonia in the employment register.

m-b85b5b3b.t: Estonia's entrepreneur account (ettevõtluskonto), under the Simplified Business Income Taxation Act in force since 1 January 2018: a natural person may open, with a credit institution resident in an EEA state, an account that receives only proceeds from services and sales of goods; the bank reserves and transfers the tax. The holder may not be registered for VAT nor act as a sole proprietor in the same or a similar field (§ 2(2)). As of 5 October 2026 the rate is 20% of the sums received (§ 4(1), in force from 1 January 2025), plus the funded-pension contribution rate for persons obliged to pay it; until 31 December 2024 it was 20% up to EUR 25,000 per calendar year and 40% on the excess.

m-b677da0d.t: The personal basic exemption in Estonia became a flat amount on 1 January 2026: § 23(1) of the Income Tax Act deducts EUR 8,400 a year from a resident natural person's income (EUR 700 a month), the earlier sliding scale being repealed. Until then the exemption was EUR 7,848 a year and shrank by formula once annual income exceeded EUR 14,400 (wording in force from 1 January 2023). The flat amount was enacted by the Act of 20 June 2023 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107) for an earlier date; its entry into force was changed to 1 January 2026 by the Act of 4 December 2024 (RT I, 20.12.2024, 2). It does not apply from the tax period in which the person reaches pension age.

m-affb070d.t: The Security Tax Act never applied to income or profit. An act adopted on 18 June 2025 (RT I, 08.07.2025, 1, in force 18 July 2025) repealed it before its income and profit parts were due to start on 1 January 2026; of its provisions only the VAT amendments of 1 July 2025 had taken effect. In its place the same act provided for raising the general income tax rate from 22% to 24% (divisor 0.76) and the entrepreneur-account rate from 20% to 22%, both from 1 January 2026 - increases that were themselves struck out on 3 December 2025 (RT I, 18.12.2025, 3) and never took effect. The repeal was timed 'not earlier than 2 July 2025', i.e. after the VAT amendment had entered into force.

m-adba4941.t: The lower corporate rate for regular dividends existed for seven years. From 1 January 2018 (RT I, 07.07.2017, 3) § 4(5) of the Income Tax Act taxed profit distributed under § 50^1 at 14%, the taxable amount being divided by 0.86, and § 4(4) set a 7% rate on such dividends in a natural person's hands. Both went on 1 January 2025 under the Act of 20 June 2023 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107), which also raised the general rate to 22%; § 4(5) in force on 5 October 2026 keeps only an 18% rate for § 47^1. A remnant stays: under § 61(68) a resident company still withholds 7% on a dividend paid to a natural person that is exempt under § 50(1^1) if the underlying profit was taxed under the old § 50^1.

m-ac1dbcca.t: Estonian social tax on an employee has a floor. Under Social Tax Act § 2(2) it is paid on the remuneration paid to an employee or official for a month 'but not on less than the monthly rate' of § 2^1, set yearly by the State Budget Act, not below the minimum wage of 1 July of the previous year. For 2026 it is EUR 886 (State Budget Act § 2(6), text RT I, 03.07.2026, 24) - a minimum social tax of EUR 292.38 a month, per the Tax and Customs Board (2025: EUR 820 and EUR 270.60; 2024: EUR 725 and EUR 239.25). § 2(3) scales the floor to time worked; § 2(4) lifts it in listed cases. § 2(2) names employees and officials, not board members: a Board example taxes a EUR 100 monthly board fee at 33%.

m-abd6341f.t: The Estonia-Cyprus income tax convention (signed 15 October 2012, in force 8 October 2013, RT II, 04.10.2013, 2; English authentic) applies to tax withheld on income from 1 January 2014 and to other taxes for fiscal years starting from then. Art. 10(1): dividends a company of one state pays to a resident of the other 'shall be taxable only in that other State', unless the holding belongs to a permanent establishment in the payer's state (Art. 10(3)). Art. 15: directors' fees 'may be taxed' in the company's state. Art. 4(3): a dual-resident non-individual is settled by mutual agreement, 'due regard being had to the place of effective management of such person or any other relevant criterion'.

m-a7ae3e79.t: A company in the Estonian commercial register files no tax registration. Taxation Act § 18(1) obliges only these to register with the tax authority before starting activity in Estonia: a legal person not in the commercial, non-profit or religious-association register; a state or municipal agency not in the state register of agencies; a non-resident whose Estonian permanent establishment is not a registered branch; an association without legal personality that incurs a tax liability in Estonia; a non-resident employer with staff working in Estonia. A board member with sole right of representation gets e-MTA access 'automatically based on the data of the commercial register'. VAT is separate.

m-a4e8b1f1.t: The Estonian Social Insurance Board (page updated 11 March 2026) on which state insures a person tied to more than one EU or EEA state or Switzerland: one state's legislation applies at a time; for work in several states the place of a substantial part of the activity decides, and if that is the state of residence, its scheme applies. A person living in Estonia and working in several states applies to the Board for Form A1; one who works in Estonia too but lives elsewhere applies in the state of residence. An A1 comes 'within the next working day' only on an electronic application meeting listed conditions (one: residence in Estonia), else within 30 days. Board members are not mentioned.

m-a4acee57.t: The basic exemption in Estonian income tax, by dated versions of Income Tax Act § 23: EUR 1,848 a year in 2015, EUR 2,040 in 2016, EUR 2,160 in 2017 - flat amounts; from 1 January 2018 EUR 6,000 a year, reduced by formula once annual income passed EUR 14,400 and reaching zero at EUR 25,200; from 1 January 2023 EUR 7,848 with the same income band; from 1 January 2026 a flat EUR 8,400 with the income-dependent reduction repealed. The 2026 reform was enacted on 20 June 2023 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107) for 2025 and its start was moved to 1 January 2026 by the act published RT I, 20.12.2024, 2.

m-a253c445.t: An Estonian company that is not VAT-registered still meets VAT when it buys services from abroad. Under Value-Added Tax Act § 21(1) an Estonian person receiving, from a foreign business not registered for VAT in Estonia, a service listed in § 10(5) - among them advertising, consultancy, accounting, legal, data-processing, financial and electronically supplied services - must register as a 'taxable person with limited liability' from the day the service is received, applying within three working days (§ 21(3)), and pays the VAT on such services itself (§ 3(5)). The same follows once intra-Community acquisitions of goods exceed EUR 10,000 in a calendar year (§ 21(2)). In force 5 October 2026.

m-9f28280a.t: An Estonian company does not register separately as an employer with the Tax and Customs Board, as far as the Taxation Act shows on 5 October 2026: § 18(1), which lists who must register with the Board before starting activity, names among employers only a non-resident employer whose employees work in Estonia. For a company in the commercial register the first act as an employer is the entry of each person's work in the employment register no later than the start of work (§ 25^2), after which pay is declared on the monthly form TSD. This is read from the scope of the two sections; no provision or Board page saying it in so many words was found.

m-9df058cf.t: Enacted for 1 January 2027 in Estonia: the VAT return absorbs both its invoice annex and the separate report of intra-Community supply. The act published RT I, 03.12.2024, 2 rewrites Value-Added Tax Act § 27 so that invoice data (same EUR 1,000 per-counterparty threshold) and intra-Community supply data (new § 27(1^5)) are shown on the return itself, replaces the ministerial 'form' of the return by a ministerial 'data composition', and repeals § 28 (the report of intra-Community supply). The deadline stays the 20th day of the following month. Status on 5 October 2026: adopted and published, not yet in force.

m-9d55c1a6.t: The Estonian Tax and Customs Board tells founders who are e-residents that an Estonian company managed from abroad will be taxed abroad as well (page last updated 4 November 2025): 'Income of Estonian companies is also taxed abroad when the management of Estonian companies occurs outside of Estonia', and 'If an e-resident manages the company from outside of Estonia, such Estonian company will probably have a permanent establishment abroad and income tax must be paid on the profit earned by this Estonian company in that foreign state.' It adds that Estonian tax residency 'does not automatically exempt companies from taxation elsewhere'.

m-9cf050dc.t: For a board member or employee of an Estonian company who lives outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland, two reliefs open to EEA residents fall away on the Estonian side as of 5 October 2026: the monthly basic exemption at withholding goes only to a natural person resident in an EEA Contracting State (Income Tax Act § 42(1)); and no A1 under Regulation 883/2004 is available, so by our reading social tax of 33% is due on a board fee unless a social security agreement says otherwise. The Tax and Customs Board lists agreements with Ukraine, Canada, Russia, Australia and Belarus; the Social Insurance Board's list also has Moldova. The funded pension contribution is withheld from no non-resident.

m-9c7851af.t: As of 5 October 2026 the income tax rate in Estonia is 22% (Income Tax Act § 4(1)). For the tax objects of § 1(2)-(4) and (6)-(8) - fringe benefits, distributed profit, gifts and non-business expenses, a permanent establishment's profit, the anti-avoidance bases - the taxable amount is divided by 0.78 before the rate is applied (§ 4(1^1)); the Tax and Customs Board writes this as 'Corporate income tax is 22/78'. Both provisions are in force since 1 January 2025, introduced by the act of 20 June 2023 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107). Read in the Estonian consolidated text RT I, 09.07.2026, 66, in force from 1 October 2026; the text enacted for 1 January 2027 (RT I, 09.07.2026, 67) keeps § 4 as is.

m-9c0b39d3.t: A café must give each paying consumer a proof of purchase. Consumer Protection Act § 4(4), as worded from 1 September 2025 (RT I, 08.07.2025, 71), obliges a trader to present the consumer a document proving the purchase when goods or a service are paid for at once; it shows at least the trader's name and place of business, the date, and each item's name, price and the amount paid (§ 4(4^1)). A paper document is given on the consumer's demand, and by default when the consumer pays in cash and uses no customer card giving electronic access to the purchase document (§ 4(4^2)). Until 31 August 2025, § 4(5) said that below EUR 20 the document was given on request; that subsection was repealed.

m-9bc1d35f.t: Both Estonia and Cyprus reserved the whole of Article 4 (Dual Resident Entities) of the OECD Multilateral Instrument, so that article does not apply to their covered tax agreements, the 2012 Estonia–Cyprus convention among them. In the lists of reservations and notifications deposited with their instruments of ratification (Cyprus: deposited 23 January 2020), each state says that, pursuant to Article 4(3)(a), it 'reserves the right for the entirety of Article 4 not to apply to its Covered Tax Agreements'. Both lists name the convention as covered, signed 15-10-2012 and in force 08-10-2013. Files read on the OECD site on 5 October 2026.

m-96747ec3.t: Estonia taxes a board member's fee from an Estonian company wherever the board member lives or works. Income Tax Act § 29(2) makes taxable the income a non-resident receives for performing the duties of a member of a management or controlling body of a resident legal person; the Tax and Customs Board's page (updated 14 November 2025) says such remuneration 'shall be taxable in Estonia regardless of where the work was actually done' and is subject to income tax (22% from 2025) and social tax (33%). Both rates stand in the Acts in force on 5 October 2026 (Income Tax Act § 4(1), Social Tax Act § 7(1)). The company declares the fee in Annex 2 of form TSD by the 10th of the month after payment.

m-93cc6747.t: Paying social tax on a board member's fee gives Estonian health insurance only on two conditions. Health Insurance Act § 5(1) insures a permanent resident of Estonia, a person living in Estonia on a temporary residence permit or right of residence, or a person legally staying and working in Estonia on a temporary basis; and § 5(2) point 4 (in force since 1 January 2016) covers a member of a management or supervisory body only where the legal person or persons pay social tax for him or her in a month on at least the monthly rate set by the State Budget Act - EUR 886 in 2026 per the Tax and Customs Board, i.e. EUR 292.38 of social tax a month. In force 5 October 2026.

m-927a1d47.t: Corporate income tax in Estonia is declared monthly, not annually: under Income Tax Act § 54(1), (2) and (4) a resident legal person files a tax return on the taxable payments and expenses of a calendar month by the 10th day of the following month and pays the tax by the same day. The return is form TSD (Declaration of income and social tax, unemployment insurance premiums and contributions to mandatory funded pension), set by Minister of Finance Regulation No 60 of 29 November 2010. The Tax and Customs Board states that dividends go into Annex 7 of form TSD and their recipients into form INF 1. In force on 5 October 2026.

m-909d65f8.t: Late payment of an Estonian tax bears interest of 0.06% a day, counted from the day after the statutory due date up to and including the day of payment or set-off (Taxation Act § 115(1), § 117(1)). When it grants payment by instalments the tax authority may reduce the rate by up to 50% from the day of its decision and, in a justified exceptional case, from the day the debt arose (§ 117(2)). In force on 5 October 2026.

m-8fc4766d.t: Under Art. 10(1) of the Estonia–Cyprus tax convention (in effect since 1 January 2014), 'Dividends paid by a company which is a resident of a Contracting State to a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State'. The exception in Art. 10(3) covers dividends effectively connected with a permanent establishment the recipient has in the paying company's state. The convention has no rate table for dividends: the source state gets no withholding right on a dividend paid to a resident of the other state.

m-8a9a316c.t: An Estonian company can pass on dividends received without paying the 22/78 tax again. Under Income Tax Act § 50(1^1) a dividend is not taxed at the paying company's level if paid out of a dividend from a taxable company resident in an EEA state or Switzerland in which the Estonian company held at least 10% of the shares or votes when it received the dividend (point 1), or from a company elsewhere on the same 10% condition where tax was withheld or the underlying profit was taxed (point 3), or out of profit of its permanent establishment in an EEA state or Switzerland (point 2) or, if that profit was taxed, elsewhere (point 4). Non-cooperative jurisdictions are excluded. In force 5 Oct 2026.

m-88ac30c8.t: Adopted by the Riigikogu on 30 September 2026 and sent to the President for promulgation on 1 October 2026; not published in Riigi Teataja as of 5 October 2026: bill 935 SE, 'Act amending the Funded Pensions Act and the Taxation Act' (Government bill of 1 June 2026). Per the adopted text it enters into force on 1 November 2026, with § 1 points 4, 7, 8 and 10-17 on 1 January 2028. From 1 November 2026 a person who stopped contributing to, or withdrew money from, the second pension pillar may resume after five years instead of ten; from 1 January 2028 money may be withdrawn before pension age in part. It bears on payroll because resuming restarts withholding of the 2%, 4% or 6% contribution.

m-84107866.t: Dated changes to Estonian VAT and payroll levies, 2015-2026. VAT: threshold EUR 16,000 to EUR 40,000 on 1 Jan 2018; press publications 5% from 1 Aug 2022; standard rate 20% to 22% on 1 Jan 2024; accommodation 9% to 13% and press 5% to 9% on 1 Jan 2025, with the EU small-enterprise scheme and a new way of counting the threshold; standard rate 22% to 24% on 1 July 2025; payment-data reporting by payment service providers from 1 Jan 2024. Payroll: social tax 33% and unemployment premiums 1.6% + 0.8% unchanged throughout; funded pension 2% with 4% or 6% by choice applied from 1 Jan 2025; minimum wage EUR 390 (2015) to EUR 946 (1 Apr 2026); social tax monthly base EUR 886 in 2026.

m-840c3106.t: Minister of Finance Regulation No 21 of 30 September 2026 (RT I, 02.10.2026, 6) amended Regulation No 60 of 29 November 2010 on tax return forms: § 1 point 2 now names, instead of Annex 1 of form TSD, the part 'Payments made to persons, withheld income tax, mandatory funded pension contribution and unemployment insurance premium, and calculated social tax and employer's unemployment insurance premium' of form TSD 'Payments'; point 3 (Annex 2, payments to non-residents) is repealed; the main form, the gifts annex and form ESD are reissued. Its own § 2 says it enters into force on 1 October 2026; it was published on 2 October and Riigi Teataja shows it in force from 5 October 2026.

m-8155ccc5.t: When an Estonian company earns profit through a permanent establishment abroad and that profit is taxed there, dividends paid out of it are exempt from the Estonian distribution tax, per the Tax and Customs Board (page updated 4 November 2025). The statute draws the line by location: for a permanent establishment in an EEA state or Switzerland the dividend is exempt if paid out of profit attributed to it (Income Tax Act § 50(1¹) 2)); for one in any other state, only if that profit 'has been taxed' (§ 50(1¹) 4)). The profit must still be reported in Annex 7 of form TSD and the recipients in form INF 1.

m-81129c51.t: Social tax on an Estonian board member's fee when the member is insured in another EU or EEA state or Switzerland - the Estonian side as the Tax and Customs Board states it: social tax is not due in Estonia 'only if the recipient of such remuneration has been issued in his or her home country a certificate of social security coverage valid in such foreign country on Form A1'. Its social tax page adds that Regulation (EC) No 883/2004 applies, that an A1 issued in another member state means no Estonian social tax liability, and that in Estonia the Social Insurance Board determines the applicable legislation and issues A1 certificates. Without an A1 the company pays 33%. Read 5 October 2026.

m-7fc62ab6.t: Estonian income tax rate (one rate for persons and for companies' distributed profit), by dated versions of § 4 of the Income Tax Act: 21% until 31 December 2014; 20% from 1 January 2015 (enacted in advance by RT I, 08.07.2011, 5), with distributed profit grossed up by dividing by 0.80; 22% from 1 January 2025 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107), divisor 0.78, i.e. 22/78 of the net distribution. The rate is 22% in the text in force on 5 October 2026 and in the consolidated text already published to apply from 1 January 2027. A rise to 24% from 1 January 2026 was enacted in June 2025 and removed in December 2025 before it took effect.

m-7ca5bb59.t: Unemployment insurance premiums in Estonia are set by Government regulation inside ranges fixed by Unemployment Insurance Act § 41: 0.5-2.8% for the insured person, 0.25-1.4% for the employer. For 2026 they are 1.6% (withheld from the employee) and 0.8% (employer) under Regulation No 78 of 25 September 2025 (RT I, 30.09.2025, 3); the same rates are already enacted for 2027-2030 by Regulation No 87 of 18 September 2026 (RT I, 23.09.2026, 8, in force 1 January 2027). Under § 3(2) of the Act a sole proprietor, and a board member to whom the Employment Contracts Act does not apply, are not insured and bear no premium. The employee's share stops at pensionable age; the employer's continues.

m-7a374e8a.t: The rate of Estonia's entrepreneur-account tax was twice scheduled to rise on 1 January 2026, and both changes were cancelled before taking effect. The Security Tax Act (adopted 11 December 2024, RT I, 02.01.2025, 2) would have added the security-tax rate to the 20%; the Act of 18 June 2025 (RT I, 08.07.2025, 1) repealed that Act and instead replaced '20' with '22' in § 4(1) from 1 January 2026; the Act of 3 December 2025 (RT I, 18.12.2025, 3) then struck that amendment out. The consolidated text in force from 1 January 2026 (RT I, 18.12.2025, 16) therefore still reads 20%, as it does on 5 October 2026.

m-77772230.t: Levies on a salary paid by an Estonian employer in 2026, as published by the Tax and Customs Board (page last updated 26 March 2026): income tax 22%, withheld from the employee; social tax 33%, paid by the employer on top of the gross salary; unemployment insurance premium 1.6% withheld from the employee (until pensionable age) and 0.8% paid by the employer; mandatory funded pension contribution 2%, or 4% or 6% if the person has applied for it, withheld only from employees in the second pillar, which covers Estonian tax residents only. All four are declared on form TSD and paid by the 10th day of the month after the payment. Taxation is cash-based: the rates of the month of payment apply.

m-7753af6e.t: Estonia's monthly payroll return changed in October 2026. Finance Minister Regulation No 21 of 30 September 2026 (RT I, 02.10.2026, 6; shown by Riigi Teataja as in force 5 October 2026, its own § 2 naming 1 October) repealed the separate non-residents' annex of form TSD and set one part 'Väljamaksed' for payments to natural persons and non-resident legal persons. Its filling rules say the state of work is entered where the person holds an A1 certificate — for wages the state where the work is done, for a management-body member's fee the state where the company is located — and that for a non-resident the applicable income tax rate is shown, the treaty rate if a residence certificate exists.

m-76b6e710.t: Estonian payroll levies on an employee's salary have no upper ceiling as of 5 October 2026: the Social Tax Act sets the rate at 33% 'of the taxable amount' (§ 7(1)) and caps the base only for a sole proprietor's business income (ten times the sum of the monthly minimum wages of the tax period, per year) and for crew of qualifying ships (EUR 750 a month, § 2(4) point 8); the Unemployment Insurance Act (§§ 40-41) and the Funded Pensions Act (§§ 7, 9) set rates without a cap. Of the 33%, 20 points go to state pension insurance and 13 to state health insurance (§ 10(2)); for a person paying the funded pension contribution the split is 16 and 13, with 4 points to the pension registrar (§ 10(4)).

m-6ed7c6c3.t: The reservations by which Estonia and Cyprus keep Article 4 of the OECD Multilateral Instrument out of their treaties had not been withdrawn as far as the depositary's list shows: the OECD's 'Signatories and Parties' table, status as of 15 September 2026, has no entry under 'Notifications made after becoming a Party' for Cyprus (signature 07-06-2017, deposit 23-01-2020, entry into force 01-05-2020) or for Estonia (signature 29-06-2018, deposit 15-01-2021, entry into force 01-05-2021). Estonia's only further entry, 01-06-2022, stands in the column of notifications under Article 35(7)(b), which concern completion of internal procedures for the Instrument to take effect for a treaty.

m-6e2df47e.t: As a rule an Estonian resident company pays no income tax on profit kept in the company: Income Tax Act § 1(3) taxes a resident legal person's profit 'upon its distribution', and under § 50(1) (in force 5 October 2026) a resident company pays tax on dividends or other profit distributions 'upon their payment in monetary or non-monetary form'; a bonus issue is not taxed. Exception: a resident credit institution pays quarterly advance tax on profit (§ 47^1). The same company-level tax falls on fringe benefits (§ 48), gifts, donations and entertainment expenses (§ 49), equity payouts above contributions (§ 50(2)), the transfer-pricing difference (§ 50(4)) and non-business expenses (§§ 51-52).

m-6bedcdb0.t: From 1 January 2026 the basic exemption in Estonian personal income tax is a flat EUR 8,400 a year (EUR 700 a month) for every resident natural person below pensionable age, whatever the income (Income Tax Act § 23(1)); from the tax year in which a person reaches pensionable age it is EUR 9,312 a year (EUR 776 a month) (§ 23^5). An employer applies it at withholding only on the person's written application, and a person may lodge it with one withholding agent (§ 42(1)-(2)). The same deduction at withholding is open to a natural person resident in another EEA state (§ 42(1) speaks of a resident of a Contracting State). In force 5 October 2026.

m-6b51b092.t: For a non-resident who works for an Estonian company entirely outside Estonia as an employee, the Tax and Customs Board states that 'there is no need to declare employment income or pay taxes on employment income in Estonia', adding that a tax liability may arise abroad. Basis: Income Tax Act § 29(1) taxes a non-resident's pay only for work in Estonia; Social Tax Act § 3 point 7 exempts pay a resident pays a non-resident for work done abroad, and Unemployment Insurance Act § 40(2) point 4 follows it. Neither covers a board member's fee (§ 29(2)). Where the pay is taxed in Estonia, an A1 from an EEA state or Switzerland removes social tax and the unemployment premium. Read 5 October 2026.

m-6433346e.t: VAT registration in Estonia is by application to the Tax and Customs Board: within three working days of the registration duty arising (Value-Added Tax Act § 20(1)); the Board registers the person within five working days of the application (§ 20(3)). A person may also apply voluntarily before the threshold is reached (§ 20(2)). In either case the applicant must prove that it carries on or is starting business in Estonia; otherwise the Board refuses (§ 20(4^1)). The Board's page for e-residents' companies adds that an Estonian company with no actual business activity and no VAT-liable transactions in Estonia 'is generally not registered for value added tax in Estonia'. As of 5 October 2026.

m-63bf8de7.t: Fringe benefits in Estonia are taxed in the employer's hands, not the employee's: the employer pays income tax at 22/78 on the value of the benefit and social tax at 33% on the benefit plus that income tax (Income Tax Act § 48(1), § 4(1^1); Social Tax Act § 2(1) point 7). 'Employee' here includes a member of the management or supervisory body and a person working under a contract under the law of obligations (§ 48(3)). Benefits are declared without naming recipients in Annex 4 of form TSD by the 10th day of the following month. Listed examples: housing costs, private use of the employer's vehicle, insurance premiums not required by law, loans below market interest. In force 5 Oct 2026.

m-5d406beb.t: Access to the Estonian Tax and Customs Board's e-MTA portal is by state authentication (TARA): the Estonian ID-card and documents equated with it (digital ID, residence permit card, e-resident's digital ID, diplomatic identity card), Mobile-ID, Smart-ID, and other EU states' eID means of high assurance level. The Board states that e-residents use its e-services 'under the same conditions as persons holding an Estonian ID-card' and that the language of tax proceedings is Estonian. A board member with sole right of representation receives the company's access packages automatically; with joint representation the members authorise a representative by a digitally signed power of attorney.

m-5c5ad310.t: When a non-resident sells shares of an Estonian company, Income Tax Act § 29(4) point 5 taxes the gain only where more than 50% of the company's assets were, directly or indirectly, Estonian immovables at the sale or within the two preceding years and the seller held at least 10%. A payment on a capital reduction, share buy-back or liquidation is taxed in a non-resident's hands above the holding's cost, save the part taxed at company level (§ 29(5), § 15(2)-(3)). The Cyprus convention agrees: gains on shares deriving over 50% of their value from immovable property may be taxed where the property lies (Art. 13(2)); other gains only in the seller's state (Art. 13(5)). In force 5 Oct 2026.

m-5bd5101f.t: Estonia's entrepreneur account (ettevõtluskonto) is a flat-tax regime for natural persons: a bank account in an EEA credit institution into which only receipts from selling goods and services are paid, with tax of 20% of every amount received reserved by the bank and passed to the Tax and Customs Board monthly; the rate rises by the person's funded pension rate if he or she is in the second pillar (Simplified Business Income Taxation Act §§ 1, 4, 6). Until 31 December 2024 the rate was 20% on receipts up to EUR 25,000 a calendar year and 40% above; the single 20% rate dates from 1 January 2025 (RT I, 19.12.2024, 1). The holder may not be VAT-registered (§ 2(2)). In force 5 October 2026.

m-5b4763f4.t: Two income-tax rises for 2026 were enacted in Estonia and both were cancelled before applying. The Security Tax Act of 11 December 2024 (RT I, 02.01.2025, 2) set a 2% 'security tax' on personal income and on company profit from 1 January 2026 until 31 December 2028. The Act of 18 June 2025 (RT I, 08.07.2025, 1) repealed it with effect from 18 July 2025 and instead raised the income tax rate from 22% to 24% (divisor 0.78 to 0.76) from 1 January 2026. The Act of 3 December 2025 (RT I, 18.12.2025, 3) then deleted that rise. Only the security tax's VAT part took effect, on 1 July 2025.

m-5b0644a8.t: Estonia and Cyprus have both placed their income tax convention under the OECD Multilateral Convention (MLI). Estonia's ratification act of 4 December 2019 (RT II, 18.12.2019, 1; consolidated text RT II, 17.12.2020, 2) lists the Estonia-Cyprus convention (signed 15 October 2012, in force 8 October 2013) among the agreements it wishes covered, and Riigi Teataja shows the MLI in force for Estonia from 1 May 2021. Cyprus's list of reservations and notifications, deposited with the OECD on 23 January 2020, names the same convention as its agreement No 15. The MLI changes a treaty only where both parties list it and their choices match; which articles apply is a separate question.

m-592a3dbc.t: The Security Tax Act (Julgeolekumaksu seadus) was adopted on 11 December 2024 (RT I, 02.01.2025, 2). As adopted it set a 2% security tax from 1 January 2026 on (a) the income of resident natural persons and non-residents' Estonian-source income, with the deductions of chapter 4 of the Income Tax Act (incl. the basic exemption) barred, and (b) the pre-tax accounting profit of resident companies and of non-residents' Estonian permanent establishments, with quarterly advance payments; the entrepreneur-account rate was to rise by 2 points. Separately, § 21 raised the standard VAT rate from 22% to 24% from 1 July 2025, to return to 22% on 1 January 2029. §§ 1-18 were to run to 31 December 2028.

m-5916af70.t: Estonian tax residence of a company turns on incorporation alone: under Income Tax Act § 6(2) a legal person 'is a resident if it is established under Estonian law' (plus a European company or cooperative whose seat is registered in Estonia); the section contains no place-of-management test. A company formed by an e-resident or other non-resident is therefore an Estonian resident. Where a tax treaty assigns residence differently, § 6(5) gives the treaty priority. The Tax and Customs Board warns that if such a company is managed from abroad it 'will probably have a permanent establishment abroad' and its profit may be taxed there. In force 5 October 2026.

m-53d17ad3.t: Estonian law does not require a private limited company to pay its management board member. Commercial Code § 180^1(1) says only that the fee and the payment procedure are set by a resolution of the shareholders (or of the supervisory board, if there is one), and § 180^1(2) that total payments must be reasonably proportionate to the member's duties and the company's economic situation. The Tax and Customs Board reads Law of Obligations Act § 28(1) as presuming that, unless otherwise agreed, a board member can expect pay, and warns that an owner-manager's choice not to pay himself 'may be based on a desire to replace active work salary with dividends and this is unacceptable under tax law'.

m-4f2a0ab5.t: The national minimum wage in Estonia is EUR 946 a month for full-time work and EUR 5.67 an hour from 1 April 2026 (Government Regulation No 36 of 23 March 2026, RT I, 24.03.2026, 5, issued under Employment Contracts Act § 29(5)). It replaced Regulation No 87 of 19 December 2024, under which the minimum was EUR 886 a month and EUR 5.31 an hour from 1 January 2025. Earlier monthly minimums listed by the Tax and Customs Board: 2015 EUR 390; 2016 EUR 430; 2017 EUR 470; 2018 EUR 500; 2019 EUR 540; 2020 and 2021 EUR 584; 2022 EUR 654; 2023 EUR 725; 2024 EUR 820.

m-4e52ac98.t: An Estonian VAT payer files a VAT return (form KMD) for each calendar month by the 20th day of the following month and pays the VAT by the same date (Value-Added Tax Act § 27(1), § 38(1)). With it goes an annex (form KMD INF) listing invoices issued to and received from legal persons, sole proprietors and public bodies at the 24%, 13% and 9% rates, where the invoices with one counterparty total at least EUR 1,000 without VAT in the period; the threshold is counted separately for sales and purchases. Intra-Community supplies of goods, and services to VAT-registered customers in other member states taxable there, go into a separate report (form VD) by the same day (§ 28). As of 5 October 2026.

m-4cf493c8.t: By contrast with a board member's fee, a salary paid by an Estonian company to a non-resident employee for work done outside Estonia is not taxed in Estonia, according to the Tax and Customs Board (page updated 4 November 2025): 'If the work of a non-resident is carried on outside of Estonia, there is no need to declare employment income or pay taxes on employment income in Estonia. Even though the employer is from Estonia, in such cases a tax liability may arise abroad.' The Board asks that payments to a sole shareholder who is also director and worker be split into salary, board fee and dividends 'according to their actual substance'.

m-40755a6d.t: Estonia's VAT registration threshold was EUR 16,000 of taxable turnover per calendar year from 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2017 and has been EUR 40,000 since 1 January 2018 (Value-Added Tax Act § 19(1), dated versions in Riigi Teataja). The way the EUR 40,000 is counted changed on 1 January 2025: before, it was taxable turnover excluding sales of fixed assets and distance sales into Estonia; since then it is the turnover defined in § 19^1(3), which also brings in real-estate, insurance and financial-services turnover unless incidental. Amount unchanged on 5 October 2026.

m-3d0c3c5a.t: For a company resident in both Estonia and Cyprus the fallback missing from their 2012 tax convention exists in EU law. Directive (EU) 2017/1852 covers disputes between Member States on the interpretation and application of double-tax conventions: an affected person may complain to both authorities within 3 years (Art. 3); they have 2 years, extendable by 1, to agree (Art. 4); failing that an Advisory Commission is set up at the person's request (Art. 6), whose opinion binds them if they still disagree (Art. 15(2)). It applies to complaints made from 1 July 2019 on tax years starting from 1 January 2018. Estonia transposed it in chapter 14¹ of the Taxation Act, in force 15 November 2019.

m-3bef9478.t: A dividend paid by an Estonian company is taxed once, at company level; nothing is withheld from the shareholder - resident or non-resident, natural or legal. Income Tax Act § 18(1) taxes a resident natural person only on dividends from a foreign legal person; § 29 lists no dividend among a non-resident's Estonian-source income; the Tax and Customs Board states that from 2025 dividends 'are only taxed at the company level in Estonia with income tax at the rate of 22/78'. One transitional exception (§ 61(68)): 7% is withheld from a natural person's dividend that the company passes on tax-exempt under § 50(1^1) out of a dividend whose profit was taxed at 14/86 before 2025. As of 5 Oct 2026.

m-3bd855d0.t: What an Estonian company pays 22/78 income tax on besides dividends and fringe benefits, with the limits in force on 5 October 2026 (Income Tax Act §§ 49, 51): gifts and donations, except goods or services handed over for advertising worth up to EUR 21 without VAT (EUR 10 until 31 December 2024); catering, accommodation, transport or entertainment of guests and business partners above EUR 50 a calendar month plus 2% of that month's payments subject to social tax (EUR 32 until 31 December 2024); and expenses unrelated to business, which include any payment lacking a source document that meets accounting rules. Both limits were raised by the act published RT I, 20.12.2024, 2.

m-3baa199c.t: Estonia's general income tax rate, which is also the corporate rate on distributed profit, moved as follows (Income Tax Act § 4(1) and (1^1), dated versions in Riigi Teataja): 21% (divisor 0.79) through 31 December 2014; 20% (divisor 0.80, i.e. 20/80) from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2024; 22% (divisor 0.78, i.e. 22/78) from 1 January 2025. The rise to 22% was enacted on 20 June 2023 (RT I, 30.06.2023, 107). A further rise to 24% (divisor 0.76) from 1 January 2026 was enacted on 18 June 2025 and struck out on 3 December 2025 before it took effect, so 22% is the rate in force on 5 October 2026.

m-38d6fc48.t: Payment services are exempt from VAT in Estonia. Value-Added Tax Act § 16(2^1) exempts, among financial services, 'payment services within the meaning of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act' (point 4) and the issue and administration of non-cash means of payment such as electronic payment instruments and e-money (point 5). A supplier that has notified the Tax and Customs Board in writing beforehand may nevertheless add VAT to these services, except when supplying a taxable person of another member state, and is then bound for at least two years (§ 16(3) point 3, (4)). The Act does not name merchant acquiring as such. In force 5 October 2026.

m-37b4ff36.t: The Estonia–Cyprus tax convention of 2012 counts 'a place of management' among permanent establishments (Art. 5(2)(a)), and under Art. 7(1) the profits of an enterprise of one state are taxable only there unless it carries on business in the other state through a permanent establishment, in which case the other state may tax 'only so much of them as is attributable to that permanent establishment'. This is the treaty footing of the Estonian Tax and Customs Board's warning that an Estonian company managed from abroad 'will probably have a permanent establishment abroad'; the convention itself does not say when a director working from home makes a place of management.

m-37808ac2.t: The Estonian Tax and Customs Board announced (page section dated 18 August 2026, in the future tense) that from 1 October 2026 salary-payment data for the monthly TSD return are sent from accounting software over a machine-to-machine interface; the Board generates the declaration and the business approves it. Annexes 1 and 2 give way to one view of salary payments for residents and non-residents, where data can still be entered manually; the old XML format ends (new: XBRL GL), CSV upload stays until the end of 2027; Annexes 3-8 are unchanged for now; the deadline stays the 10th. Legal basis: Minister of Finance Regulation No 21 of 30 September 2026 (RT I, 02.10.2026, 6).

m-35917d3a.t: The Estonia–Cyprus tax convention of 15 October 2012 breaks a dual residence of a company by agreement, not by a rule: under Art. 4(3), where a person other than an individual is resident of both states, 'the competent authorities of the Contracting States shall settle the question by mutual agreement due regard being had to the place of effective management of such person or any other relevant criterion'. Art. 4(1) counts as a resident a person liable to tax by reason of domicile, residence, place of management, place of incorporation or a similar criterion. The convention sets no fallback for the case where the authorities do not agree.

m-32310d8d.t: No change of income tax rates, of the corporate 22/78 rate or of the basic exemption is enacted for 1 January 2027 in Estonia as of 5 October 2026. The consolidated Income Tax Act published for 1 January 2027 (RT I, 09.07.2026, 67) differs from the text in force (RT I, 09.07.2026, 66) in four sections only: § 5 (the share of personal income tax passed to local governments), § 13 and § 19 (allowances connected with military service) and § 37 (suspended activity of a sole proprietor, notary or bailiff). §§ 4, 23, 48-54 are identical in both.

m-30a90ad3.t: Estonia's mandatory funded pension (second pillar) contribution is withheld only from Estonian tax residents. Funded Pensions Act § 6 defines the obligated person as a resident natural person under Income Tax Act § 6(1); the rate is 2% unless the person has chosen 4% or 6% (§ 9, option in force since 1 January 2024, first applied from 1 January 2025). The Tax and Customs Board says (page of 6 January 2025) that a non-resident's earnings - then declared in Annex 2 of form TSD, since October 2026 in its 'Payments' part - are not subject to the contribution, and that only employees obliged to join or joined voluntarily take part; withholding starts or stops on 1 January, 1 May or 1 September.

m-307463ab.t: The Estonian Tax and Customs Board's published position on dividends in place of pay (advice page last updated 1 November 2023, framed as general practice, not a binding assessment): 'A shareholder is entitled to dividends but the dividend may not replace salary.' Where a shareholder who is also board member or employee is paid at or near the level usual in the industry, the Board sees no tax risk; where pay is significantly lower or at minimum wage while profit goes out as dividends, it sees a risk needing detailed analysis and, if a dividend is found to have replaced salary, 'a basis for reclassification of dividend income to salary and applying social tax and payments'.

m-2d439177.t: Estonia-Cyprus income tax convention (RT II, 04.10.2013, 2, English text) on pay and relief. Article 14(1): salary of a resident of one state 'shall be taxable only in that State unless the employment is exercised in the other Contracting State'; even then (Article 14(2)) only the residence state taxes if the person spends no more than 183 days in the other state in a twelve-month period, the employer is not its resident and the pay is not borne by a permanent establishment there. Article 15 lets Estonia tax directors' fees of an Estonian company. Article 21(2): Cyprus allows Estonian tax paid 'as a credit against Cyprus tax', up to the Cyprus tax on that income. In force 5 Oct 2026.

m-284b91a0.t: VAT rates in force in Estonia on 5 October 2026 (Value-Added Tax Act § 15): standard rate 24% of the taxable value; 13% on accommodation or accommodation with breakfast; 9% on books and educational literature (physical or electronic), on medicines, contraceptives, sanitary and hygiene products and medical devices for disabled persons listed by ministerial regulation, and on press publications (physical or electronic, other than those mainly carrying advertising, private classifieds, erotic or pornographic content, or video or music content); 0% on exports and intra-Community supplies of goods, among others.

m-27d7283f.t: Estonia applies the EU payment-data reporting for VAT (CESOP) through Value-Added Tax Act § 36^1, in force since 1 January 2024 (act published RT I, 21.11.2023, 1). A payment service provider that in one quarter provides payment services for more than 25 cross-border payments to the same payee must keep and send to the Tax and Customs Board data on the payee and the payments (payee name, VAT or other identifier, IBAN, date, amount, refunds and others); records are kept electronically for three calendar years; the data go to the Board for each quarter by the end of the following month through its e-service. The duty lies on the provider, not on the merchant.

m-26ee62a6.t: Taxes that meet an Estonian OÜ selling online or over a counter, as in force on 5 October 2026 (Estonian texts read). VAT: registration becomes compulsory on the day turnover with Estonia as place of supply exceeds EUR 40,000 from the start of the calendar year (Value-Added Tax Act § 19(1), wording in force since 1 January 2025). Income tax: the rate is 22% (Income Tax Act § 4(1), in force since 1 January 2025), and a resident company pays it on profit distributed as dividends or other profit distributions 'upon their payment' (§ 50(1)), the taxable amount being divided by 0.78 before the rate is applied (§ 4(1^1)).

m-1e0a2711.t: Enacted for 1 January 2027: the Act amending the Social Tax Act and related acts, adopted 20 May 2026 (RT I, 03.06.2026, 2). It adds a tax object, § 2(1) point 6^1 - fees a natural person receives from a natural person under a contract for services, taxed under the sole-proprietor rules - and an exemption, § 3 point 21: pay from a non-resident employer to a non-resident employee with health insurance for the first 183 days of work in Estonia, unless the payer is resident in an EEA state, Switzerland or a state with a social security agreement with Estonia, or the pay is for agency work. The 33% rate is untouched. Status on 5 October 2026: published, not yet in force.

m-19a27abc.t: Riigi Teataja's English translations of Estonia's two main tax acts lag the Estonian text as of 5 October 2026. The latest English Income Tax Act is the version in force 9 May-30 September 2026 (translation published 8 May 2026); the latest English Value-Added Tax Act is the version in force 1 January-30 September 2026. Both are shown as no longer in force, and the Estonian texts in force from 1 October 2026 have no translation yet. The 1 October changes touch only Income Tax Act § 19 and Value-Added Tax Act § 39 (references to the new crisis and national defence act), so rates, exemptions and deadlines read the same in both languages.

m-16b611f2.t: Estonia's standard VAT rate changed twice in two years (Value-Added Tax Act § 15(1), dated versions in Riigi Teataja): 20% from 1 July 2009 to 31 December 2023; 22% from 1 January 2024 (act published RT I, 01.07.2023, 2); 24% from 1 July 2025 (Security Tax Act, RT I, 02.01.2025, 2). The 24% rate was enacted as temporary, with a return to 22% on 1 January 2029, but that reversal clause fell with the repeal of the Security Tax Act on 18 July 2025; the rate has no end date in the text in force on 5 October 2026 or in the text enacted for 1 January 2027 (RT I, 30.06.2026, 130).

m-16afda30.t: What is fixed and what is only proposed for Estonian payroll in 2027, as of 5 October 2026. Enacted: unemployment insurance premiums stay 1.6% and 0.8% in 2027-2030 (Government Regulation No 87 of 18 September 2026); the Social Tax Act changes on 1 January 2027 (act of 20 May 2026, RT I, 03.06.2026, 2) for fees between natural persons and for non-resident employers' staff, the 33% rate untouched. Proposed: the 2027 State Budget bill (1037 SE, introduced 29 September 2026) sets the monthly rate for minimum social tax at EUR 946, up from EUR 886 in 2026 - the lowest Social Tax Act § 2^1 allows, the minimum wage being EUR 946 on 1 July 2026. No 2027 change of the 22% income tax rate is enacted.

m-15c68180.t: The rise of Estonia's income tax rate to 24% planned for 1 January 2026 was cancelled before it took effect. An act adopted on 3 December 2025 (RT I, 18.12.2025, 3) struck §§ 1 and 3 and § 4(1) out of the act of 18 June 2025, i.e. both the 24% general rate (with 24/76 for companies) and the 22% entrepreneur-account rate. As a result, on 5 October 2026 the income tax rate is 22%, the corporate rate 22/78 and the entrepreneur-account rate 20%; the consolidated Income Tax Act enacted for 1 January 2027 (RT I, 09.07.2026, 67) keeps § 4 unchanged.

m-142760c6.t: The Estonia–Cyprus tax convention removes double taxation by different methods on each side (Art. 21). Estonia exempts: where a resident of Estonia derives income which under the convention 'has been taxed in Cyprus', Estonia exempts it, and may take it into account when computing tax on the rest. Cyprus credits: 'subject to the provisions of Cyprus Tax Law regarding credit for foreign tax', Estonian tax paid in accordance with the convention on income derived from Estonia is allowed as a credit against Cyprus tax, capped at the Cyprus tax on that income. For a Cyprus resident's board fee taxed in Estonia under Art. 15, the relief therefore lies with Cyprus.

m-13212b5c.t: Estonia's reduced VAT rates were reshuffled on 1 January 2025 by the act published RT I, 01.07.2023, 2: accommodation, taxed at 9% from 1 January 2009 to 31 December 2024, moved to a separate 13% rate (Value-Added Tax Act § 15(1^1)); press publications, taxed at 5% from 1 August 2022 to 31 December 2024 (§ 15(2^1), introduced by RT I, 04.06.2022, 4), moved to 9% (§ 15(2) point 5). The 9% rate on books and listed medicines was not changed. Status on 5 October 2026: 13% and 9% in force.

m-12049740.t: The ministerial instrument for Estonia's 2027 VAT return exists: Minister of Finance Regulation No 19 of 28 September 2026 'Käibedeklaratsiooni andmekoosseis' (Data composition of the VAT return), RT I, 02.10.2026, 19, issued under Value-Added Tax Act § 27(1), in force 1 January 2027. It sets four parts - main form KMD, issued and received invoice data KMD INF, report of intra-Community supply VD and its amendment report VDP - applies them to taxable periods beginning from 1 January 2027, and repeals Regulation No 17 of 10 June 2014 (VAT return form) and Regulation No 69 of 28 December 2009 (forms of the intra-Community supply report). Status on 5 October 2026: published, not yet in force.

m-0c574eeb.t: A business must register for Estonian VAT once its turnover with place of supply in Estonia exceeds EUR 40,000 in a calendar year; the duty arises that day (Value-Added Tax Act § 19(1), in force 5 October 2026). Since 1 January 2025 the turnover counted is that of § 19^1(3): taxable supplies incl. zero-rated, real-estate, insurance and financial services, less sales of fixed assets and incidental transactions. No duty arises if the year's turnover is all exempt and zero-rated supply (other than intra-Community supply of goods). A foreign business with no fixed establishment in Estonia has no threshold: it registers from its first taxable supply the customer does not reverse-charge (§ 19(3)).

m-0adf4600.t: The person providing work - an Estonian or a non-resident legal person, among others - must register each worker in the employment register kept by the Tax and Customs Board no later than the moment work starts; suspension and termination within ten days (Taxation Act § 25^2). The register covers persons whose work creates a tax liability in Estonia - employees, service providers under a contract under the law of obligations, members of a legal person's management or supervisory body - and persons working unpaid in a company's economic interests (§ 25^1(4)-(5)). Channels: e-MTA, X-tee, a service bureau; by phone or SMS only the start, to be completed within seven calendar days (§ 25^4(3)).

m-0a4f3692.t: Proposed, not adopted as of 5 October 2026: Government bill 994 SE 'Act amending the Income Tax Act and, in connection with it, other acts', introduced in the Riigikogu on 14 September 2026, first reading completed 28 September 2026, amendments due by 12 October 2026. It replaces the ministerial 'forms' of tax returns with ministerial 'data compositions' in the Income Tax, Social Tax, Unemployment Insurance and Funded Pensions Acts and makes Estonian residents file the withholding and social tax return (TSD) electronically whatever the number of recipients, paper only with the tax authority's leave. Proposed commencement: 1 December 2026; e-filing duty 1 January 2027. No tax rate is touched.

m-09709db5.t: Dated changes to Estonian income tax, 2015-2026, from the acts in Riigi Teataja. 1 Jan 2015: rate 21% to 20% (companies 20/80). 1 Jan 2018: basic exemption EUR 2,160 to EUR 6,000 a year, income-dependent; 14/86 rate for regular dividends with 7% withheld from natural persons; loans to shareholders taxable as hidden distributions (§ 50^2). 1 Jan 2023: basic exemption EUR 7,848. 1 Jan 2025: rate 20% to 22% (companies 22/78); 14/86 and 7% repealed; entrepreneur account 20% flat. 18 July 2025: Security Tax Act repealed before applying to income or profit. 1 Jan 2026: basic exemption flat EUR 8,400; the enacted rise to 24% struck out on 3 Dec 2025.

m-05cdfb8e.t: A transitional rule keeps one trace of Estonia's former lower dividend rate alive in 2026: under Income Tax Act § 61(68) a resident company withholds 7% from a dividend or other profit distribution paid to a natural person where that dividend is exempt at company level under § 50(1^1) and the underlying profit was taxed under the 14/86 rule in force until 31 December 2024. The Tax and Customs Board adds that such a dividend may be passed on tax-free to a corporate shareholder if the company passing it on held at least 10% of the payer when it received it, and that a tax treaty may free a non-resident natural person from the 7% (Cyprus is on the Board's list) or cut it to 5%.

m-012a4736.t: Outline (i), same online shop - stage 4, taxes, as of 5 October 2026. VAT: registration is compulsory once turnover with Estonia as place of supply passes EUR 40,000 in the calendar year, and may be requested at founding; goods sent to consumers in other EU states stay taxed in Estonia only while such sales exceeded EUR 10,000 neither last year nor this year. Income tax: the company pays it on profit distributed as dividends, upon payment - 22% of the amount divided by 0.78. The board member's fee is taxed in Estonia although he lives abroad: income tax withheld at 22% and social tax at 33%, the latter not due, per the Tax and Customs Board, if he holds an A1 certificate from his home state.

m-f770ac25.t: New registrations and filing discipline in Estonia, as reported by ERR on 22 January 2026 from commercial-register data: 28,329 entities ('ettevõte' in ERR's wording; evidently legal entities of all forms) were entered in the commercial register in 2025, 28,786 in 2024 and 26,120 in 2023; 67% of obliged entities filed the annual report for financial year 2024 by the deadline, and 45,920 had still not filed it on 22 January 2026. The register's statistics pages add that over 20,000 private limited companies have been established annually since 2016 and that for 94.9% of legal entities (2024 financial year) the financial year ends on 31 December, so the report is due on the last day of June.

m-f52622ec.t: How payment of an Estonian OÜ's capital is shown to the registrar, as of 5 October 2026: a notice from a credit institution or payment institution is attached to the registration application only if the contribution exceeds EUR 50,000; where the cash contribution is not over EUR 50,000 the management board members confirm in the application that the contributions have been paid to the company (Commercial Code § 144(1) 3) and § 144(2¹), in force from 1 February 2023). Under § 520(4) the payment account the founders open in the name of the company being founded may be with a credit or payment institution established in any EEA state or its branch in an EEA state (wording of 1 January 2019).

m-f4655a11.t: Form of an Estonian annual report, 5 October 2026: it comprises annual accounts and a management report, but a micro-undertaking applying the Estonian financial reporting standard may prepare annual accounts only (Accounting Act § 14(1), (1¹)); it is drawn up in Estonian (§ 25(1)); at least one executive-management member signs it once approved (§ 25(3)). Under § 25(4), in force from 17 January 2025 (RT I, 07.01.2025, 1) and applied to reports for periods beginning from 1 January 2024 (§ 62(23)), no e-signature need be added when the report is prepared, approved and filed through the e-Business Register and approver and filer are securely identified; not so for a report subject to audit.

m-f4428635.t: Whom an Estonian OÜ must engage by law, as of 5 October 2026 (synthesis): a notary - to found it outside the expedited procedure, to transfer or pledge a share unless the articles waive the notarial form, and to certify any register application not signed digitally; a contact person from the closed list of Commercial Register Act § 24(4) - only if its address is abroad; an auditor - for the annual accounts only above the thresholds of Auditors Activities Act §§ 91-92 or if the articles require, and to check a contribution in kind from EUR 25,000; an accountant - never, the Accounting Act not saying who keeps the books; a company secretary or resident director - no such office or condition.

m-f2952964.t: Three Estonian public sources describe the contact-person duty in the wording repealed on 1 February 2023. On 5 October 2026 the e-Residency site ('If your Estonian company's management board address is located abroad, then the Commercial Code requires…'), its knowledge base (updated 29 October 2025: 'as required by the Commercial Code') and the Tax and Customs Board's page for e-residents (updated 4 May 2026: 'if the management board of a company or the body substituting it is located in a foreign country') all cite the Commercial Code and the board's location, while the rule in force is § 24(2) of the Commercial Register Act and its trigger is the legal person's address abroad.

m-f1a88136.t: Since 15 January 2018 the seat (asukoht) of an Estonian legal person in private law is 'the place in Estonia determined by the partnership agreement or the articles of association, unless otherwise provided by law' (General Part of the Civil Code Act § 29(1¹), inserted by RT I, 20.04.2017, 1); until 14 January 2018 § 29(1) defined the seat of any legal person as the location of its management board or the body replacing it, also unless otherwise provided by law. The seat thus stays in Estonia whoever manages the company. That the address may be abroad is not stated as a permission; it is inferred from § 24(2) of the Commercial Register Act, which requires a contact person in that case.

m-eda7f109.t: Estonian OÜs founded without paid-in capital under the regime repealed on 1 February 2023 remain under a transitional rule, Commercial Code § 520¹ (in force from 1 February 2023; text as of 5 October 2026): a shareholder who has not paid the contribution in full is liable to the company for its obligations up to the unpaid amount where the obligation cannot be met from the company's assets; until all shareholders have paid in full the company may neither increase nor reduce its share capital nor make any payout to shareholders, a ban that does not cover salary or other remuneration; an agreement releasing a shareholder from paying has no effect against third parties.
