m-ec928d95.t: Scale of register deletions in Estonia, as reported by ERR on 22 January 2026 from commercial-register data: in 2025, 12,687 entities ('ettevõte' in ERR's wording) were deleted, 4,764 of them as a result of supervision - over 4,550 for an unfiled annual report and 212 for a missing contact person; in 2024, 38,783 were deleted, over 31,000 by supervision. 846 legal persons were reinstated in 2025 and 1,558 in 2024. The counts evidently cover legal entities of all forms, not companies only: the register's own page says 9,969 more legal entities were deleted than established in 2024 (ERR's figures give 9,997) and links the jump to the Commercial Register Act in force from 1 February 2023.

m-e9ec3eb0.t: How capital is handled on the Estonian e-Business Register portal, per the Centre of Registers' guide dated 27 October 2025 (read 5 October 2026): 'The minimum capital ... is 0.01€ (if there is one shareholder)' and each shareholder's share is at least EUR 0.01; for capital of no more than EUR 50,000 the applicant confirms that all contributions have been made 'outside the portal', and for capital above EUR 50,000 the money is paid to a court deposit account and reclaimed to the company's account after registration. The guide gives the state fee for founding an OÜ electronically as EUR 265.

m-e88ae52a.t: Other Estonian commercial-register state fees as in force on 5 October 2026 (State Fees Act §§ 62-63, amounts in force since 1 January 2022 unless noted): entering a sole proprietor (FIE), general or limited partnership EUR 20 (EUR 13 in 2015-2021); entering a change for an OÜ or AS EUR 25 (EUR 18 in 2015-2021); a change for a sole proprietor EUR 10 (EUR 4 in 2015-2021); double rate for a change entered on a fixed date (from 1 March 2024); reservation of a business name EUR 150 (§ 62¹, in force from 1 March 2024); restoring to the register a legal person deleted for a missing annual report or missing contact person EUR 200 (§ 62(4), from 1 February 2023).

m-e69d2a59.t: Estonia's e-Residency programme page 'Start a company' (read 5 October 2026) lists four steps with its own cost and time figures: prepare; 'Get a contact person - 200 - 400 € / year - online - 1 day - 1 week'; 'Register your company - 265 € - online - 15 min - 1 hour'; 'Open a bank account - 0 - 200 € - online - 1 hour - 1 week'. It says a company needs 'either a legal address or a contact person service from licensed service providers', that both services are administrative and give no right to act for the company, and that the best option for e-residents is a business account with a neobank based in the EEA.

m-e4523b37.t: State fee for entering an Estonian OÜ in the commercial register, as in force on 5 October 2026: EUR 200, or EUR 265 when the entry is made on an expedited-procedure application (State Fees Act § 62(2)); both amounts date from 1 January 2022 (amending Act RT I, 08.12.2021, 1). From 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2021 the same subsection set EUR 145 and EUR 190. The texts published for 1 November 2026, 1 January 2027 and 1 July 2027 keep EUR 200 and EUR 265.

m-ddf4e27d.t: Typical first-year costs as the e-Residency programme itself publishes them (knowledge-base article 'Costs & fees', updated 29 October 2025, read 5 October 2026): e-Residency application EUR 150 (state fee; card valid 5 years, same fee for renewal); registering an OÜ EUR 265; contact person 'on average' EUR 200-400 per year; accounting 'from EUR 50 per month'; total first-year rough costs 'ca EUR 600 (DIY)' or 'ca EUR 1300 (with accounting support)'. The article 'strongly recommend[s]' a professional accountant and notes that an annual report is mandatory for all Estonian companies even if they have not been active.

m-d51a9105.t: Advertised prices of a second Estonian vendor, Xolo OÜ (product 'Xolo Leap', pricing page read 5 October 2026, vendor's own figures, 'all prices excluding VAT'): bundled plans including help with online company registration, a virtual office (legal address and PO box), accounting, Estonian tax reporting and the annual report cost EUR 59 per month ('Starter', for the first 12 months or until revenue reaches EUR 4,000), EUR 99 ('Standard'), EUR 139 ('Pro') and from EUR 259 ('Premium'); extras include EUR 200 for late annual-report processing. On the same date the e-Residency Marketplace showed 47 providers and 79 packages under its filter for legal address and contact person services.

m-cd7fa82c.t: The state fee for entering a private limited company in the Estonian commercial register, read in dated versions of the State Fees Act: EUR 145, or EUR 190 on an expedited-procedure application, in every version checked from 1 January 2015 to 6 January 2020; EUR 200, or EUR 265 expedited, from 1 January 2022 (amended by RT I, 08.12.2021, 1) and unchanged in the version in force on 5 October 2026. The same amounts apply to a public limited company, a commercial association and a branch of a foreign company; a sole proprietor's entry costs EUR 20 from 1 January 2022.

m-cd2b026d.t: An Estonian company must appoint a contact person in Estonia when its address is in a foreign state (Commercial Register Act § 24(2), in force since 1 February 2023). Only a notary, an advocate or law-firm operator, a sworn auditor or audit firm, a non-resident's tax representative, or a licensed trust and company service provider may be appointed (§ 24(4)); documents delivered to the contact person count as delivered to the company and that person's address counts as the company's address (§ 24(7)). A company that fails to appoint one may be struck off after a warning and three further months (§ 62).

m-ccb28be3.t: Estonia's contact-person rule in three dated versions. Until 14 January 2018 Commercial Code § 63¹(2) made an OÜ name a person with an Estonian address for service if at least half of its board members did not reside in Estonia, another EEA state or Switzerland. From 15 January 2018 (RT I, 20.04.2017, 1) a 'contact person' was compulsory when the management board 'is located in a foreign state'; only listed professionals could be appointed, but a board member, shareholder or procurator residing in Estonia could also be (§ 63¹(3)). From 1 February 2023 § 63¹ was repealed; § 24 of the Commercial Register Act ties the duty to the legal person's address being abroad and has no such exception.

m-c239a2e3.t: Since 1 February 2023 the founders of an Estonian OÜ must pay for their shares in full before the application for entry in the commercial register is filed (Commercial Code § 140(2), wording of RT I, 05.05.2022, 1). Until 31 January 2023 the clause ended 'unless the memorandum of association provides otherwise', and § 140¹ (in force 1 January 2011 - 31 January 2023) let an OÜ with planned capital of not more than EUR 25,000, founded only by natural persons, be set up without paying in, the shareholders being liable for the company's obligations up to the unpaid amount where the company's own assets did not suffice. § 140¹ was repealed from 1 February 2023.

m-c22ecb79.t: Deletion of an Estonian company for a missing annual report, in force since 1 February 2023: after the legal deadline the registrar sets a time limit for filing with a warning of deletion, which may be sent automatically; the company may be deleted if it has not filed within that limit and at least three months have passed since the statutory filing date (Commercial Register Act § 61). Deletion also requires that the registers show no assets, that no court, criminal or enforcement proceedings are pending, consent of the authorities named by the minister, and a notice in Ametlikud Teadaanded at least three months before (§ 60(2), (5)). Restoration can be sought within three years (§ 64(2)).

m-c0f2a506.t: In the Estonian e-Business Register a holder of another EU state's eID can log in, but cannot sign: the Centre of Registers' help page (dated 12 November 2025) says EU eID tools allow login 'to view the data', while 'statements and reports can only be signed by logging in with an Estonian ID card (including e-residency card), Estonian smart ID or Estonian mobile ID'. Its portal page (read 5 October 2026) makes electronic establishment of a company conditional on all related persons being able to sign with one of those Estonian tools.

m-bc78322c.t: E-invoicing in Estonia in two dated versions of § 7¹ of the Accounting Act. From 1 July 2019 (RT I, 15.03.2019, 3) a seller had to present a machine-readable invoice (e-invoice) when supplying the state, local authorities, legal persons in public law and entities they control. From 1 July 2025 (RT I, 10.10.2024, 1) any accounting entity that wants to receive only e-invoices has itself marked as an e-invoice recipient in the commercial register, and such a buyer may require the seller to present an e-invoice, presumed proper if it meets European standard EN 16931-1 unless the parties agree another standard. The Act lays down no general duty to issue e-invoices to every business customer.

m-bb43550f.t: Without an Estonian eID a founder of an Estonian private limited company goes through a notary: the memorandum of association and the articles must be notarially authenticated and signed by all founders, and a founder's representative may sign only under a power of attorney that is notarially certified (Commercial Code § 138(4), wording in force since 1 January 2011; a sole founder signs a notarially authenticated foundation resolution, § 138(5)). Estonian text read, version in force from 1 March 2024 (RT I, 06.07.2023, 131), shown as currently valid on 5 October 2026.

m-b4c0b98a.t: A contact person of an Estonian company is entered for a stated term: the registrar must be given the term and told of its extension, and 'on expiry of the term the contact person's data are removed from the commercial register automatically' (Commercial Register Act § 24(6), as in force on 5 October 2026); the entry needs the contact person's signed consent (§ 24(5)). Per the Centre of Registers (page of 7 November 2025) a contact person can itself notify the register that it no longer acts and ask for its data to be removed. For a company whose address is abroad either event leaves it without the compulsory contact person - the ground for deletion under § 62.

m-b37c4076.t: A share-capital contribution paid as a deposit to the registrar's account when an Estonian company is founded must be claimed back: the company applies, no later than one year after its registration, for the money to be returned to its payment account with a credit or payment institution established in an EEA state or a branch there; after that the contribution stays in state revenue. A correct application is paid within five working days (Commercial Code § 520(4¹), as in force on 5 October 2026). If the company is never registered, the deposit is returned by court order and stays with the state if no application reaches the court within two years of payment (§ 520(5)).

m-b2e13e3b.t: The e-Residency programme's knowledge base (article updated 15 December 2025, read 5 October 2026) states that after an OÜ registration application is submitted online 'the review process usually takes one business day', and that a company 'can only be registered online if all founders, board members etc. have an Estonian e-Residency digital ID card, an Estonian ID card, an Estonian mobile ID or Estonian Smart ID'; otherwise, or for a subsidiary of a foreign company, 'you need to use the services of a public notary office in Estonia'. The Centre of Registers' help pages give '1-5 working days' for the registrar to review change applications.

m-b09e484d.t: To found an OÜ online, every person named in the application must sign it digitally in the e-Business Register portal: the Centre of Registers' guide (dated 27 October 2025, read 5 October 2026) says the application 'can be signed only with Estonian ID card (inc. e-residency card), Smart-ID and mobile-ID', and its login page (12 November 2025) says other EU eID tools let a user log in only to view data. A board member living in another EU state who holds none of these cannot sign in the portal with a home-state eID. The guide gives the state fee for founding an OÜ electronically as EUR 265 and the minimum capital as EUR 0.01 with one shareholder.

m-af0a23b6.t: An Estonian OÜ needs a supervisory board only if its articles of association prescribe one (Commercial Code § 189(1), wording in force since 1 January 2011), and an auditor only where the Auditors Activities Act or the company's articles impose an audit of the annual accounts (§ 190(1)). The Code has no office of company secretary: a search of the consolidated text in force on 5 October 2026 finds the word 'sekretär' once, and not as an organ of a private limited company. The only compulsory organ besides the shareholders is the management board (§ 180(1)).

m-acd2a939.t: Data in Estonia's e-Business Register 'has been accessible to everyone free of charge' since 1 October 2022, according to the register's own statistics page (read 5 October 2026); the register's price list on that date shows a single paid item, public-file documents of non-profit associations at EUR 2, and refers to Regulation No 2 of the Minister of Justice of 4 January 2023. The Commercial Register Act still says the issue of electronic register data is subject to a fee of up to two euros per query set by ministerial regulation, with web queries about oneself and about valid registry-card data exempt (§ 32(1)-(3)).

m-a8bba7cc.t: Deleting an Estonian company for a missing annual report became faster on 1 February 2023. Under Commercial Code § 60 (in force until 31 January 2023) the registrar acted once the report was six months overdue, set a time limit of at least six months with a warning of deletion, could then publish a notice in Ametlikud Teadaanded inviting creditors to seek liquidation within six months, and only then delete. Under § 61 of the Commercial Register Act (from 1 February 2023) the registrar sets a time limit once the deadline has passed and may delete when at least three months have passed since the statutory filing date, after a notice published at least three months before deletion (§ 60(5)).

m-a34db4ae.t: In an Estonian OÜ the body answerable for bookkeeping is the management board: 'The management board organises the accounting of the private limited company' (Commercial Code § 183; text as of 5 October 2026), and after the end of the financial year the board draws up the annual report in the manner laid down in the Accounting Act (§ 179(1)). Neither provision requires the board to engage an accountant or sets a qualification for whoever keeps the books.

m-9ec5a9be.t: Address and contact rules for an Estonian company, as in force on 5 October 2026: the registry card shows seat, address and e-mail address (Commercial Register Act § 12 p 5); an address is given to the precision of a building or part of one registered in the address data system (§ 10(3)), a foreign address with state and administrative unit (§ 10(4)); a management board member, liquidator or OÜ shareholder who is not a data subject of the Estonian population register must give the registrar a contact address and e-mail address and report changes at once (§ 10(5)). If the registrar cannot reach the company by the details given, it may publish a notation of contact difficulties (§ 55).

m-9da5c3c0.t: Statutory elements of an Estonian notary's fee for founding an OÜ, as in force on 5 October 2026 (Notary Fees Act): the transaction value of a memorandum or foundation resolution is the planned share capital, but not less than EUR 127 nor more than EUR 639,116 (§ 18(1), (5)); the fee is one 'full fee' from the table in § 22 for a unilateral act and twice the full fee for an act of two or more parties (§ 23) - the full fee for a value up to EUR 128 is EUR 6; drafting an application to the registration department, certifying the applicant's signature and issuing a digital copy costs a fixed EUR 35.75, plus EUR 6.35 for each further signatory (§ 31 p 9¹). VAT is added.

m-95456ba4.t: As of 5 October 2026 Estonian law sets no minimum share capital for a private limited company (osaühing, OÜ). § 136 of the Commercial Code, as worded from 1 February 2023 by the Act of 13 April 2022 (RT I, 05.05.2022, 1), says only that share capital is expressed in euros; until 31 January 2023 it added that share capital must be at least 2,500 euros. § 148(1) makes one cent the smallest nominal value of a share since 1 August 2020 (RT I, 17.03.2020, 1); before that it was one euro.

m-91da230d.t: From 1 January 2011 an Estonian private limited company (osaühing) could be founded without paying in its share capital: § 140^1 of the Commercial Code (inserted by RT I 2010, 77, 589) let founders, if all natural persons and planned capital up to EUR 25,000, agree that shares need not be paid for on foundation. Until he paid, a shareholder was liable to the company for its obligations up to the unpaid amount where its assets could not meet them, and the company could not change its capital or pay shareholders anything but wages and other remuneration. Minimum capital stayed EUR 2,500 (§ 136). § 140^1 was repealed on 1 February 2023; § 520^1 keeps these rules for companies so founded.

m-9192c0c3.t: The Estonian company registration portal used to accept several foreign eIDs for signing and no longer says so. In the Centre of Registers' page archived on 18 August 2019, registration applications could be submitted 'by persons having an Estonian, Latvian, Belgian or Finnish ID card or Estonian or Lithuanian Mobile ID'; on 5 October 2026 its portal page says applications and reports 'can only be signed with an Estonian ID-card, Smart-ID, and Mobile-ID'. The date and instrument of the change were not found.

m-892bd316.t: The legal basis of free access to Estonia's e-Business Register, as in force on 5 October 2026: Regulation No 2 of the Minister of Justice of 4 January 2023 (RT I, 19.01.2023, 1, in force from 1 February 2023, issued under § 32(2) and (4) of the Commercial Register Act) charges no fee for the electronic issue of registry-card data, other data shown in the register and public-file documents, including download in XML, JSON or XBRL (§ 8(1)); the one fee is EUR 2 per query for a public-file document of a non-profit association (§ 8(2)). Anyone may make free single queries by a legal person's name or registry code (§ 2(3)).

m-85f3e9d9.t: What the Estonian commercial register records for an OÜ, as of 5 October 2026: on the registry card, among other data - name, registry code, legal form, seat, address and e-mail address, contact person, names and personal codes of management board members, financial year (Commercial Register Act § 12), plus the amount of share capital and the list of shareholders with the nominal value of each share (§ 13 p 1 and 4, § 14; shareholders on the card since 1 September 2023). The planned main field of activity is notified on registration under the Estonian classification of economic activities (EMTAK) and kept in the public file (Commercial Code § 4(5); Commercial Register Act § 26(1) p 3).

m-812a744d.t: An Estonian annual report that needs no audit can be approved on the e-Business Register without any signature: since 17 January 2025 Accounting Act § 25(4) (Act RT I, 07.01.2025, 1) requires no e-signature where the report is prepared, approved and filed through the register and the approver and filer are securely identified. Per the Centre of Registers' page 'Electronic confirmation' (dated 2 April 2025, read 5 October 2026), 'if the users of a foreign authentication tool can also authenticate through eu ID and prepare the report, they can also use the electronic approval option', while a report that must be audited, reviewed or revised must still be digitally signed.

m-800f89c0.t: The statutory review periods behind advertised registration times in Estonia: the registrar reviews an entry application within five working days of receipt (Commercial Register Act § 41(3)); in the expedited procedure the application is reviewed no later than the next working day after receipt, an application arriving after the end of a working day, on a day off or on a public holiday counting as filed on the following working day (§ 42(2)). A period restarts when the application is amended or a further document is filed. Estonian text in force from 1 January 2025 (RT I, 14.03.2025, 10).

m-7fc2a319.t: Commercial Code § 520(4¹), in force on 5 October 2026 and untouched by the 2023 reform, says that in the expedited procedure the cash contribution on founding is made as a deposit to the registrar's account or to the account of § 27(2) of the anti-money-laundering Act. A company that paid to the registrar's account must apply within one year of registration for its return to its payment account with an EEA credit or payment institution (wording of 1 January 2019); after that it stays in state revenue. A correct application is paid in five working days. Since 1 February 2023 § 144(2¹) of the Code and § 42(3) p 4 of the Commercial Register Act call for the deposit only above EUR 50,000.

m-7d5abdfd.t: The sole proprietor (füüsilisest isikust ettevõtja, FIE) in Estonian law as in force on 5 October 2026: any natural person may be one, and must apply for entry in the commercial register before starting activity (Commercial Code § 3(1)-(2)); the state fee is EUR 20 (State Fees Act § 62(1), unchanged since 1 January 2022 and in the versions enacted up to 1 July 2027). A sole proprietor is an accounting entity (Accounting Act § 2(2)), may keep accounts on a cash basis and, on either basis, has no duty to prepare an annual report (§ 43(1)-(3)). The Code sets no capital for a sole proprietor, and the limitation of liability in § 135(2) concerns shareholders of an OÜ only.

m-796877a7.t: Estonia's Commercial Register Act (Äriregistri seadus) was adopted on 13 April 2022, published as RT I, 05.05.2022, 1, and entered into force on 1 February 2023, with parts on 1 August 2023, 1 September 2023 (shareholder list on the registry card) and 1 March 2024 (entries on a fixed date, business-name reservation) (§ 104). The same publication removed the EUR 2,500 minimum capital of an OÜ and founding without paying in, moved the contact-person rule out of the Commercial Code, and introduced deletion from the register for a missing annual report or contact person, with restoration within three years. All legal persons in private law are entered in the one commercial register (§ 3(1)).

m-77c47d47.t: Estonian notaries offer remote authentication by video link, but participants sign the deed with a digital signature (Notarisation Act § 13(7)), and the Chamber of Notaries names only Estonian means for entering its portal and signing: 'a Republic of Estonia ID card, digital ID, mobile ID, Smart ID or an e-Resident's digital ID' (page dated 20 January 2023, read 5 October 2026). It is at the notary's discretion and, per the Chamber, covers all notarial acts except marriage and divorce. The Notary Fees Act § 2(2¹) adds EUR 20 to the notary's fee for it, VAT on top; the Chamber's 'EUR 24 including VAT' dates from the 20% rate, and VAT is 24% since 1 July 2025.

m-7647ce04.t: When Estonia dropped the minimum share capital on 1 February 2023 it also ended founding without payment: § 140(2) of the Commercial Code, as amended by RT I, 05.05.2022, 1, says founders must pay for their shares in full before the registration application is filed. Proof depends on the amount: where a monetary contribution does not exceed EUR 50,000 the management board members confirm in the application that it has been paid (§ 144(2^1)); a notice from a credit institution or payment institution is attached only if the contribution is over EUR 50,000 (§ 144(1) p 3). § 141 still has founders open a bank account in the name of the company being founded for monetary contributions.

m-71617338.t: A board member of an Estonian company without Estonian digital identity can still get the annual report filed, per the Centre of Registers' guide 'Options for foreign residents' (24 August 2021; paper approval is still listed on the signing page of 7 November 2025): where no board member is registered with an Estonian personal identification code, someone able to log in to the portal - the board member or an accountant - enters the data, prints the report, has the board sign it and uploads the scan; an audited report goes the same way with the auditor's signed report. Since 2025 a board member logging in with an EU eID may instead approve an unaudited report electronically.

m-6d6df492.t: Who can file on Estonia's e-Business Register portal, per the Centre of Registers' help page dated 12 November 2025 (read 5 October 2026): a user logs in with an Estonian ID-card, Mobile-ID or Smart-ID; EU eID tools let one 'enter to view the data', but 'statements and reports can only be signed by logging in with an Estonian ID card (including e-residency card), Estonian smart ID or Estonian mobile ID'. A citizen of another EU state with only a foreign eID therefore cannot sign a registration application on the portal; an e-resident can. For an annual report needing no audit or review, the same site's page of 2 April 2025 lets an EU-eID user approve it electronically without signing.

m-6be443ee.t: Outline (ii), café in Tallinn run by an OÜ with a resident owner - stage 1, company and bank, as of 5 October 2026. The owner signs the founding application in the e-Business Register portal with an Estonian ID-card, Mobile-ID or Smart-ID; state fee EUR 265; capital from EUR 0.01; employees can be entered in the same application. Bank: Swedbank opens a business account in its Internet Bank, contracts signed by Smart-ID, Mobile-ID or ID-card, and charges EUR 0 for the account, euro payments and a debit card in the first year; SEB's plans cost EUR 1 to EUR 15 a month, free for a year for a new business customer opening by 30 November 2026; LHV opens and maintains the account free of charge.

m-67a3bc99.t: Conditions of the expedited registration procedure for an Estonian OÜ (Commercial Register Act § 42(3), as of 5 October 2026), among others: the documents are digitally signed by the persons who must sign them - the person himself or herself or a legal person's statutory representative; the standard articles of Commercial Code § 139¹ are used; the registrar can verify the personal data of founders and board members automatically; only cash contributions are made, and a contribution over EUR 50,000 has reached the registrar's deposit account or the account of § 27(2) of the anti-money-laundering Act; the shares are not in the Estonian securities register; the state fee has been received.

m-6567ef99.t: Advertised prices of one Estonian company-formation vendor, Unicount OÜ (pricing page read 5 October 2026, vendor's own figures): company formation EUR 296 including VAT, of which EUR 265 is the state fee and EUR 31 the vendor's fee, claiming registration 'in 1 working day'; 'virtual office' - registered office address and contact person in Estonia - EUR 199 per year plus VAT; accounting plans EUR 29 per month plus VAT for software only ('Lite') and EUR 99 per month plus VAT with an accountant ('Micro'); standalone annual accounts for a dormant company from EUR 199. The vendor states that its formation service is available only with its annual virtual-office or contact-person subscription.

m-6230e36c.t: The contact-person duty for Estonian companies run from abroad dates from 15 January 2018: § 63^1 of the Commercial Code (added by RT I, 20.04.2017, 1) made a company whose management board 'is located in a foreign state' appoint a contact person in Estonia - only a notary, advocate, law office, sworn auditor, audit firm, non-resident's tax representative or trust and company service provider (until 20 July 2020 also a notary's office) - unless a board member, shareholder or procurist living in Estonia took it. Since 1 February 2023 the rule is § 24 of the Commercial Register Act: the trigger is 'if the address of the legal person is in a foreign state', and the insider exception is gone.

m-6101e0a9.t: Estonian penalty for a late annual report, as in force on 5 October 2026: if a legal person has not filed its annual report within the statutory time limit, the registrar may, without first issuing a warning order, impose the fine of § 601 of the Code of Civil Procedure repeatedly until the report is filed, taking into account how many times and for how long the report has been overdue (Commercial Register Act § 57(1)-(2), in force from 1 February 2023). Under § 46(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure such a fine may be up to EUR 3,200.

m-5bf43db7.t: For an Estonian private limited company (OÜ) whose shares are paid by a cash contribution of not more than EUR 50,000, no bank document goes to the registrar: under § 144(2^1) of the Commercial Code (RT I, 05.05.2022, 1, in force 1 February 2023; current on 5 October 2026) the board members confirm in the registration application that the contributions have been paid to the company. A notice from a credit institution or payment institution is attached only where the contribution is over EUR 50,000 (§ 144(1) 3)).

m-536e3a46.t: The name step in Estonia involves no compulsory prior approval. The e-Business Register's 'Name search' shows identical and similar registered names and trademarks; per the Centre of Registers it 'does not give a definite answer' - the registrar decides during registration. By law a company's business name must be clearly distinguishable from names entered or reserved in the Estonian commercial register, carry 'osaühing' or 'OÜ' at its beginning or end, and be written in the Estonian-Latin alphabet (Commercial Code § 9(2)-(4), § 11(2), § 12(8)). Since 1 March 2024 a person may reserve one name for six months, for a stated legal form and field of activity, for a EUR 150 state fee (§ 15¹).

m-4c2fb9c3.t: Outside the expedited procedure the founding documents of an Estonian OÜ go through a notary: the memorandum of association and the articles approved with it must be notarially authenticated and signed by all founders, a representative needs a notarially certified power of attorney, and a sole founder signs a notarially authenticated foundation resolution instead (Commercial Code § 138(4)-(5)). The application to the registrar must be notarially certified or digitally signed; signatures may also be certified by a foreign official, in which case the document must be legalised or carry an apostille unless a treaty provides otherwise (Commercial Register Act § 40(1)).

m-4942cc96.t: An Estonian OÜ may be founded by one or more persons, natural or legal (Commercial Code § 137). Its management board has one or more members; a member must be a natural person with active legal capacity and need not be a shareholder (§ 180(2)). The Code's part on the OÜ (§§ 135-220), as in force on 5 October 2026, sets no condition of Estonian residence or of nationality for a founder or board member. § 180(3)-(3¹) bars from the board: supervisory board members; persons the articles exclude; persons under a court ban on acting as a board member or on business; persons forbidden to act in the company's field of activity; and persons barred from board membership by law or court decision.

m-440418b7.t: On entry in the Estonian commercial register a legal person receives a unique registry code (Commercial Register Act § 22(1)). The registrar notifies the applicant of the entry without delay and, as notification, sends the party an uncertified printout of the valid entries of the register (§ 43(2)-(3)); certified printouts are obtainable from a notary's office (§ 31(2)). The Act, as in force on 5 October 2026, provides for no certificate of incorporation: the words for such a document were not found in §§ 22, 31 or 43, which are the provisions on what is given out.

m-40045ee7.t: The Centre of Registers' guide to establishing an OÜ on the e-Business Register (dated 27 October 2025, read 5 October 2026) states that every person added to the application - founders, board members, a contact person - 'must be able to digitally sign the application on the portal', and that it 'can be signed only with Estonian ID card (inc. e-residency card), Smart-ID and mobile-ID'. If the company's address is in a foreign country the foreign address is entered and a contact person must be added in the same application. The application can also carry a request for voluntary VAT registration and the registration of employees, forwarded to the Tax and Customs Board on entry.

m-3b600fa5.t: Time limit in the law for an Estonian commercial register entry, as in force on 5 October 2026: an application is reviewed within five working days of its arrival (Commercial Register Act § 41(3)); the period restarts when the application is amended or a further document is filed, runs again for five working days after defects are remedied (§ 41(4)), and the registrar may extend it up to three months for circumstances needing special verification (§ 41(5)). In the expedited procedure the application is reviewed no later than the next working day after arrival (§ 42(2)).

m-3a3882c5.t: Where the founders of an Estonian OÜ may hold the account for cash contributions, in two dated versions of Commercial Code § 520(4): until 31 December 2018 'a bank account in an Estonian credit institution' in the name of the company in formation (wording in force since 1 January 2011); from 1 January 2019 (Act of 5 December 2018, RT I, 20.12.2018, 1) 'a payment account in a credit institution or payment institution established in a Contracting State of the European Economic Area, or in a branch of such an institution opened in a Contracting State'. The same Act made § 520(4¹) return a registrar-held deposit to such a payment account (before: 'its account in a credit institution').

m-277ef0ca.t: Outline (i), online shop run by an OÜ whose only board member lives in another EU state - stage 1, registration, as of 5 October 2026. (1) Signing in the portal needs an Estonian ID-card, Mobile-ID or Smart-ID; lacking these, one route is the e-resident's digital ID: state fee EUR 150, decision within 30 days, 2-5 weeks to the pick-up point, collected in person, restricted for citizens of twelve listed states. (2) In the e-Business Register portal he enters name, activity, address (and a contact person if the address is abroad), board, founder, capital from EUR 0.01 and beneficial owner, signs digitally and pays the EUR 265 state fee. (3) A voluntary VAT registration request may go with it.

m-27203a0c.t: The minimum fine for a late annual report in Estonia was dropped on 1 February 2023. Until 31 January 2023 Commercial Code § 71(2)-(2¹) let the registrar fine without a warning order where data required by law were not filed in time, the fine being 'to the extent provided in the Code of Civil Procedure, but not less than 200 euros' (wording of 19 December 2012). § 71 was repealed from 1 February 2023 (RT I, 05.05.2022, 1); § 57 of the Commercial Register Act, which replaced it for annual reports, names no minimum and tells the registrar to weigh how often and for how long the report is overdue. The EUR 3,200 ceiling of § 46(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure dates from 1 January 2011.

m-24e11520.t: An Estonian company whose address is abroad and which has not appointed the compulsory contact person receives from the registrar a time limit with a warning of deletion; it may be deleted if it does not appoint one within that limit and at least three months have passed since the date set (Commercial Register Act § 62). The registrar may instead initiate compulsory dissolution, giving at least one month to cure (§ 58(1) p 3, (2)). Providing trust and company services - which include providing a seat or business address - requires an activity licence decided by the Financial Intelligence Unit (Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Act § 8 p 3, § 70(1) p 2, § 71(1)).

m-23f3e669.t: Since 1 February 2020 an Estonian notary may authenticate acts remotely by video link, all parties signing digitally (Notarisation Act § 1(3¹), § 13(7); Act RT I, 22.02.2019, 2); Notary Fees Act § 2(2¹) adds EUR 20 before VAT (EUR 24.80 with VAT on the Chamber of Notaries' Estonian page; its English page: EUR 24). Per the Chamber (English page of 20 January 2023, read 5 October 2026) it covers all notarial acts except marriage and divorce, at the notary's discretion, and documents are signed in the self-service portal with an Estonian ID-card, digital ID, Smart-ID, Mobile-ID, residence-permit card or an e-resident's digital ID. A founder holding none of these cannot use the remote route.

m-22bb4ef7.t: Estonian law names the place for a cash contribution before an OÜ is registered: a payment account in the name of the company in formation with an EEA credit or payment institution (Commercial Code §§ 141, 520(4)) or, in the expedited procedure, a deposit with the registrar or on the start-up account of AML Act § 27(2) (§ 520(4¹)). Up to EUR 50,000 nothing checks it: the board only confirms payment (§ 144(2¹)), a received deposit is required only above EUR 50,000 (Commercial Register Act § 42(3) p 4), and the Centre of Registers' guide (27 October 2025) asks only to confirm payment 'outside the portal'. No source read on 5 October 2026 says what a founder does who cannot open one.

m-2138b216.t: An Estonian OÜ's management board must file the approved annual report with the commercial register within six months of the end of the financial year, together with the proposal for distributing profit or covering loss, a breakdown of sales revenue by field of activity (EMTAK), and the sworn auditor's report where audit is compulsory (Commercial Code § 179(4), (6)). If the shareholders do not adopt a resolution approving the report, the board files the unapproved report with a note to that effect. The financial year is 12 months and is the calendar year unless the articles provide otherwise (Accounting Act § 13(1), (3)).

m-20718568.t: State fees behind an online OÜ founding and an e-resident's card, per the State Fees Act text in force on 5 October 2026: entering a private limited company in the commercial register costs EUR 200, or EUR 265 when entered on an expedited-procedure application (§ 62(2), wording in force since 1 January 2022); review of an application for an e-resident's digital ID costs EUR 150 (§ 272(6), in force since 1 January 2025), not refunded when the application is left without review (§ 15^1 point 1). The three later versions already published - in force from 1 November 2026, 1 January 2027 and 1 July 2027 - leave § 62 and § 272(6) as they are.

m-17659090.t: Under § 24 of the Estonian Commercial Register Act (in force from 1 February 2023; text as of 5 October 2026) a legal person may appoint a contact person to whom its procedural documents and declarations of intent can be delivered in Estonia, and must appoint one if its address is in a foreign state. In that case only a notary, advocate, law-office operator, sworn auditor, audit firm, non-resident's tax representative or a trust and company service provider named in § 8 of the anti-money-laundering Act may be appointed (§ 24(4)). A document delivered to a registered contact person counts as delivered to the legal person, and that person's address is then also deemed its address (§ 24(7)).

m-11b90fe0.t: The e-Business Register guide for founding an OÜ (dated 27 October 2025, read 5 October 2026) lists what is entered: principal activity (EMTAK code), name, an address chosen from the Estonian address system or, if the company's address is abroad, a foreign address plus a contact person, an e-mail address, board members and founders, capital, articles and beneficial owners. 'As a rule, it is not necessary to add mandatory documents.' Capital of up to EUR 50,000 is confirmed as paid outside the portal. The applicant may add a request for voluntary VAT registration and entries of employees, which are forwarded to the Tax and Customs Board once the company is entered.

m-113ae101.t: The trigger of the Estonian contact-person duty changed on 1 February 2023. Until 31 January 2023 Commercial Code § 63¹(2) required a contact person 'if the management board of the company or the body substituting for it is located in a foreign state'; that section was repealed by RT I, 05.05.2022, 1 with effect from 1 February 2023, and the Commercial Register Act § 24(2) now ties the duty to the legal person's address being abroad. Companies had until 30 April 2023 to bring contact-person data into line (Commercial Register Act § 69).

m-10e0fe3f.t: Digital identities able to sign on Estonia's company registration portal, per archived snapshots of the Centre of Registers' page: 5 January 2016 - 'an Estonian, Portuguese, Belgian, Finnish or Lithuanian ID card'; 18 August 2019 - 'an Estonian, Latvian, Belgian or Finnish ID card or Estonian or Lithuanian Mobile ID'; 16 January 2021 - Estonian and Latvian ID-cards and Estonian and Lithuanian Mobile-ID, with Finnish and Belgian cards and Smart-ID for login only; 2 April 2023 - only 'an Estonian ID-card or Estonian Mobile ID', EU eID tools and Smart-ID login-only. The help page of 12 November 2025 allows signing with an Estonian ID-card (including the e-residency card), Smart-ID or Mobile-ID.

m-102fef46.t: Under § 40(1) of the Estonian Commercial Register Act an application to the registrar must be notarially certified or digitally signed; signatures may also be certified by a foreign official entitled to verify the signatory's identity, and a document certified abroad must be legalised or carry an apostille unless an international agreement provides otherwise. A person entitled to sign may authorise another, by a power of attorney in the same form as the application (§ 40(2)). Estonian text in force from 1 January 2025 (RT I, 14.03.2025, 10).

m-0fa45311.t: Transfer of a share in an Estonian OÜ, as in force on 5 October 2026: the disposition must be notarially authenticated and the notary notifies the registrar within two days (Commercial Code § 149(4)); since 1 September 2023 the transfer is deemed to have taken place from the entry in the list of shareholders in the commercial register (§ 149(4¹), Act RT I, 05.05.2022, 1), the list being kept in the register itself (§ 182(1)). Since 1 August 2020 a company whose share capital is at least EUR 10,000 and fully paid may, by unanimous shareholders' vote, waive the notarial form in its articles and allow transfers in a form reproducible in writing (§ 149(6), Act RT I, 17.03.2020, 1).

m-0c7cad58.t: In Estonia's expedited procedure an OÜ uses standard articles of association laid down by ministerial regulation; they replace both the memorandum of association and ordinary articles, state the share capital as a fixed amount, are digitally signed by all founders, and the company cannot add provisions of its own to them (Commercial Code § 139¹(1)-(4), in force since 1 January 2007). A company in a field of activity where the law requires additional data in the articles cannot use them (§ 139¹(5)).

m-06cc54b3.t: When the notary route is compulsory for founding an Estonian OÜ (reading of Commercial Code § 138(4)-(5), § 139¹ and Commercial Register Act § 42(3)-(4) as in force on 5 October 2026): a notarially authenticated memorandum or foundation resolution is needed whenever the expedited procedure is closed - among other cases: non-standard articles, a contribution in kind, shares in the Estonian securities register, a founder or representative whose data the registrar cannot check automatically (e.g. a foreign legal person), signature by an attorney, or a founder or board member unable to sign digitally. In the expedited procedure no notary and no lawyer is required by law.

m-06859840.t: Two more commercial-register state fees with dates, from the Estonian State Fees Act in force on 5 October 2026: reserving a business name costs EUR 150 (§ 62^1, a step that exists since 1 March 2024, introduced by RT I, 05.05.2022, 1), and entering a change for a private limited company, public limited company, commercial association or branch of a foreign company costs EUR 25 (§ 63(2), amount in force since 1 January 2022, RT I, 08.12.2021, 1); for an entry made on a fixed date the fee is double (§ 63(4), since 1 March 2024). The three texts already published for 1 November 2026, 1 January 2027 and 1 July 2027 keep the name-reservation fee at EUR 150.

m-fb786b39.t: The 'connection with Estonia' test entered LHV Pank's General Conditions in 2023. The version effective 13.01.2018 has no such clause. The version effective 06.05.2023 lists as a valid reason to refuse a payment service agreement that the person 'is a non-resident and does not have a reasonable interest in concluding a payment service agreement and/or does not have a sufficient link to Estonia'. The version effective 09.10.2025 (current on 5 October 2026) lets the bank refuse a person who 'is a non-resident and/or does not have a legal basis for staying in Estonia' or has 'no sufficient connection with Estonia', and makes the latter a ground to end a legal entity's agreement without notice.

m-f4e77ff3.t: SEB Pank's business 'service plans' cost per month (read 5 October 2026): Basic EUR 1, Standard EUR 2, Standard+ EUR 4, Premium EUR 6, Premium+ EUR 15, each with unlimited current accounts and 1,000 to 3,500 free intra-bank and European electronic payments; all but Basic include Mastercard Business debit cards without monthly fee. A new business customer opening its first account gets a plan free for a year (offer block: 'by 30 November 2026'; the table footnote names no end date). Plans are not concluded with non-resident legal persons - per SEB's FAQ, entities registered outside Estonia; an Estonian company represented or owned by non-resident private persons pays a document handling fee.

m-f4dd0e3e.t: SEB's Estonian contract documents already carry the name of the merged bank. The bank's page 'Terms and conditions of current account agreement' (read 5 October 2026) lists two current editions: one in force from 01.06.2026 to 31.12.2026, headed AS SEB Pank, and one in force from 01.01.2027, whose header reads 'SEB Bank AS', Tornimäe 2, Tallinn, with Finantsinspektsioon named as supervisory authority. The General Terms valid as of 01.06.2026 still name AS SEB Pank. Finantsinspektsioon had announced on 22 May 2026 that the merger of SEB's Baltic subsidiaries into SEB Bank AS 'will be completed in early 2027'.

m-f305eb02.t: LHV's non-resident price list (valid as of 1 May 2024, read 5 October 2026) charges an application fee and a monthly fee by residence. Private persons: Estonian citizens and residents free; residents of EU member states, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland EUR 100 and EUR 10 a month; residents of other countries EUR 200 and EUR 20. Legal entities: registered in Estonia free; registered in Estonia with non-resident owners EUR 300 and EUR 30; registered in an EU member state 'except Cyprus, Luxembourg, Malta' or in Norway EUR 300 and EUR 30; registered in another country - on this wording, Cyprus included - EUR 600 and EUR 60. The application fee is not refunded on refusal.

m-f2e2178c.t: Luminor Bank AS's Estonian price list for private clients valid from 01.01.2024 (archive snapshot of 4 August 2025) opened an account free of charge for residents of the European Economic Area and charged EUR 250 for checking the current-account application and documents of persons who are not residents of the European Union, the EEA or Switzerland, plus an additional maintenance fee of EUR 15 a month for a non-resident of the EEA. Its footnote counts as a resident a private person entitled to reside in those states under EU or national law, including an asylum seeker or refugee. Whether these amounts stand on 5 October 2026 could not be read: the live site answers with a bot check.

m-f1c47a96.t: AS SEB Pank's General Terms valid as of 01.06.2026 treat business clients - defined as 'a self-employed person, legal person, branch, notary or bailiff' - differently from private clients: amendments to the terms, product conditions and price list are announced one month ahead on the website and in branches, whereas private clients get two months' notice on a durable medium for payment and deposit conditions (clauses 18-19); in justified cases the price list may be amended without prior notice, except payment-service prices for private clients (20); the bank may ordinarily cancel an open-ended agreement on one month's notice to a business client and two months' to a private client (117).

m-e77f4691.t: Across the four Estonian banks whose terms were read on 5 October 2026 (LHV, Swedbank, SEB, Coop Pank) one pattern holds for an Estonian company with a non-resident owner or board member: opening needs a documented 'connection with Estonia' (registration alone is nowhere listed as enough); a non-refundable fee is paid before the decision (EUR 300 at LHV and Swedbank, EUR 500 at SEB, EUR 200 or 500 at Coop); a monthly charge follows (EUR 30 at LHV, EUR 50 at Swedbank for Cyprus-, Liechtenstein- or non-EEA-linked owners, EUR 20 or 100 at Coop); and remote opening needs an Estonian ID card, passport or residence permit - LHV states that the e-resident's digital ID is not an identity document.

m-e52408be.t: Swedbank AS's terms for a business customer on 5 October 2026: under the Current Account Agreement terms effective 31.08.2026 the bank may unilaterally change the agreement, fees and interest (the Price List) on one month's notice to a legal person and two months' to a private client (12.1), and may ordinarily cancel a legal person's agreement on one month's notice (13.3); under the General Conditions it may 'with good reason' change the Price List and Service Conditions without advance notice (1.2.4). A transfer cannot be contested after 13 months (8.5), with no shorter period for legal persons. Complaints: 15 days; Estonian law and the court of the bank's location apply (10.2).

m-dfb782e6.t: Under the Commercial Code as amended from 1 February 2023 (RT I, 05.05.2022, 1; text in force on 5 October 2026) the founders of an OÜ must pay for their shares in full before the application for entry in the commercial register is filed (§ 140(2)), and a notice from a credit institution or payment institution confirming payment of the share capital is attached to the application only 'if the contribution is over 50,000 euros' (§ 144(1) 3)). The same act repealed § 140^1, which had allowed founding an OÜ without making contributions, and reduced § 136 to one sentence: share capital is expressed in euros.

m-d7299f9d.t: Estonia's right to a basic payment account sits in § 710^1 of the Law of Obligations Act, there since 10 January 2017 (RT I, 31.12.2016, 1); text read: version in force from 1 September 2026. A credit institution must provide basic payment services to 'a consumer who lawfully resides in the European Union' and, 'in the case of justified interest of a consumer', conclude a basic payment service contract; it answers within ten settlement days and must refuse on the grounds of § 42(1) of the AML act. The right belongs to consumers only: a company has no basic-account right, and § 733^14(6) lets even the general duty to contract of § 710^1(1) be excluded for non-consumers.

m-d6c49499.t: AS SEB Pank's price list (effective 01.06.2026) opens a current account free of charge but takes a non-refundable 'handling fee of documents submitted for current account opening' from legal entities: nothing for a resident of Estonia, 'except for legal persons registered in Estonia, represented by a non-resident or whose ownership structure or ultimate beneficial owners include a non-resident' - those pay EUR 500 together with residents of other EEA states; residents of other countries pay EUR 750. The monthly current-account fee for a legal entity is EUR 1 for a resident of Estonia, EUR 20 for a resident of an EEA member state and EUR 60 for a resident of another country.

m-d6185a93.t: Coop Pank AS's published risk-appetite summary (last update 28.02.2025) states: 'E-residents are classified as non-resident clients.' Non-resident also means an Estonian company more than 25% owned or otherwise controlled by non-residents, or one where 'the majority of the company's management consists of non-residents'. 'Any non-resident who wishes to establish a business relationship must have a strong connection to Estonia', the criteria being assessed collectively - meeting one 'may not be considered a sufficiently strong connection'. It does not serve adult-entertainment businesses, virtual-currency service providers or entities registered in or owned from a high-risk third country.

m-d0f61cba.t: AS SEB Pank gives a business client three months to contest a payment. Its Terms and Conditions of Current Account Agreement valid as of 01.06.2026 (the edition its website lists as in force 01.06.2026-31.12.2026) say a private client reports a payment made without consent or executed incorrectly no later than 13 months after the debit, while a business client does so 'no later than within three months from the date the Account was debited' (clause 69). Ordinary cancellation by the bank follows its General Terms: two months' notice to a private client, one month's to a business client (clause 117). The edition valid as of 01.01.2027 keeps clause 69 and names SEB Bank AS.

m-ce665332.t: A Government bill pending in the Riigikogu on 5 October 2026 would spell out who may pull bank-account data. Bill 924 SE, initiated on 21 May 2026, amends the Taxation Act, the AML act and the act implementing the Code of Civil Procedure and the Code of Enforcement Procedure: per its official summary it specifies the rights of the Tax and Customs Board and the Financial Intelligence Unit to obtain data 'above all on bank accounts and account data', states expressly that the tax authority may demand information from credit institutions in tax proceedings, banking secrecy included, and specifies which data it may ask through the Enforcement Register channel. First reading ended 8 June 2026.

m-bf59ece2.t: Outline (i), same online shop - stage 2, the settlement account, as of 5 October 2026. The three large banks price the non-resident element: Swedbank EUR 300 for due diligence; SEB EUR 500 for handling documents (EUR 0 until 30 November 2026 where the non-resident shareholders are EEA residents); LHV EUR 300 plus EUR 30 a month where owners are non-resident. None is returned on refusal; all three weigh the link to Estonia; LHV identifies non-residents in person. The alternative is an account abroad - Wise Europe SA (Belgian law) or Paysera LT: Stripe lists EUR payouts of an Estonian account to banks in 32 countries, Belgium, Lithuania, Cyprus included, and accepts Wise and Revolut accounts.

m-be954995.t: Since 15 July 2025 (RT I, 08.07.2025, 4) an Estonian bank may not refuse a consumer a basic payment account because of its risk appetite: § 710^1(5^1) of the Law of Obligations Act says it 'may not refuse to enter into a basic payment service contract on the basis of the risk appetite' set under § 10 of the AML act, but may mitigate risk by capping monthly payments, single transactions and the balance, and by restricting cash withdrawals outside the EEA; the limits do not cover payments of taxes, fines or state fees and may not make the account unusable. Proof of justified interest 'must not be unreasonably burdensome' (2^1); in a dispute the bank bears the burden of proof (14).

m-bb5da3d5.t: Swedbank AS's checklist of account-opening documents (effective 26.03.2026) asks an Estonian legal person 'with non-residential connections' for: identity documents of the legal representatives; a CV of the non-resident representative and/or owner; agreements or contracts with Estonian business partners; a business plan or short description of the company; and, if necessary, a document identifying the beneficial owner. Such accounts are not opened directly at a branch: the bank 'will take into account the business links with Estonia (business partners/business activity in Estonia)' and decides within 10 working days after the enhanced due diligence fee is paid and all documents are in.

m-b586a85f.t: A business registered in the EEA, Estonia included, contracts for a Wise Business account with Wise Europe SA, a Belgian company (no. 0713.629.988, Brussels) authorised by the National Bank of Belgium as a payment institution; its Business Customer Agreement ('Last updated: 7 August 2026', read 5 October 2026) is governed by Belgian law, with disputes brought in the courts of Belgium, and counts a sole trader or freelancer as a business customer. Wise's Estonian price page states, as of 5 October 2026: registering free; account details for receiving in 22 currencies a one-off EUR 50; receiving domestic EUR payments free; receiving a EUR Swift payment EUR 2.39.

m-b47db532.t: Revolut's Business Terms for Estonia, as archived on 19 July 2025 (version applying from 27 February 2025), are an agreement between 'the company or sole trader' and Revolut Bank UAB, a Lithuanian bank (company no. 304580906, authorisation code LB002119) licensed by the Bank of Lithuania and the ECB; clause 31 chooses the laws of the Republic of Lithuania. An account can be opened only by a company or sole trader registered in its local government business register and, where relevant, fully incorporated; merchant services fall under a separate Payment Processing Services Agreement. The live page returned a security check on 5 October 2026, so the version in force that day was not read.

m-b35a98dd.t: AS SEB Pank's General Terms moved from a non-resident test to a 'justified interest' test. Valid from 01.06.2015 (3.1.7): the bank may refuse a non-resident natural or legal person 'who according to the Bank's opinion does not have a demonstrable connection with Estonia'. From 01.12.2016 (clause 47, from 13.01.2018 clause 48) it may refuse a basic payment service agreement to a person with 'no justified interest in and connection with Estonia'. Valid as of 01.06.2026 (48.2): a business has justified interest in particular if its owners are Estonian residents or its activity is 'largely related to Estonia' (a production unit, employees or partners there, or Estonia as a main target market).

m-ab210e27.t: Estonia's bank-account register function is carried by the Enforcement Register (täitmisregister) of § 63 of the Code of Enforcement Procedure. § 81 of the AML act obliges every credit and financial institution that opens an IBAN payment account or lets a safe-deposit box to make available through that register the holder's name, personal or registry code and address, the persons authorised to use the account, the holder's beneficial owner, and the IBAN with opening and closing dates - for open accounts and those closed in the previous five years. The duty applies since 10 September 2020 (§ 104^2), first via the electronic seizure system and since 1 January 2024 via the Enforcement Register.

m-a8d8bb26.t: AS SEB Pank's business current-account page (read 5 October 2026): 'We only start client relationships with legal persons who have a connection to Estonia' - the owners are residents of Estonia, business activity is connected to Estonia (production units, clients or partners there), or investments in Estonia (real estate). If the board members are non-residents, 'you will be asked to submit documents proving the company's connection to Estonia', such as partnership or rental agreements. '10 banking days' for reviewing documents stands in the section for non-resident legal persons; the bank's FAQ says about 20 minutes in most cases and 'up to 10 working days' if more documents are checked.

m-a8204b1c.t: LHV Pank's price list (section 'Non-residents', 'Valid as of 01.05.2024', read 5 October 2026) charges a legal entity registered in Estonia nothing for opening or keeping an account, but one 'with non-resident owners' - at least 25% held by foreign legal entities or non-resident private persons, or a non-resident ultimate beneficiary - an account opening application fee of EUR 300 and EUR 30 a month; a company registered in another EU state (except Cyprus, Luxembourg, Malta) or Norway EUR 300 and EUR 30; elsewhere EUR 600 and EUR 60. The application fee is not refunded if the bank declines. The fee does not apply to Estonian citizens living abroad.

m-a801576f.t: Coop Pank AS's Standard Terms and Conditions of Settlement Contract (applying to agreements concluded from 01.06.2026 and, from 01.08.2026, to earlier ones) give a legal entity two months to contest a payment: it 'does not have the right to file claims and objections' unless it notified the bank within two months of the debit (clause 11.1.4), against 13 months for a consumer (11.1.3). The bank may amend the service terms, price list included, unilaterally on at least two months' notice to a consumer and 'a corporate client at least one (1) month in advance' (12.2.1) - longer than the 15 days of its General Terms, which yield to service conditions that set a longer period.

m-a49fd900.t: LHV's page 'Non-residents' (read 5 October 2026) tells a business client: 'your company will need to prove a clear connection to Estonia and a need to open an account here'; a location-independent company registered in Estonia submits an overview of its activities and clients. Listed for a company registered in Estonia: application, passport copies of board members and of beneficial owners holding over 25%, overview of the ownership structure, account statement for the last 12 months. 'Non-resident clients can not be digitally identified', so LHV asks for an office visit unless the person was already identified at LHV. The e-resident's digital ID 'is not an identity document'.

m-a2985d22.t: SEB's price list effective 1 June 2026 (read 5 October 2026) charges a handling fee for the documents of a legal entity's first current account: free for a resident of Estonia, 'except for legal persons registered in Estonia, represented by a non-resident or whose ownership structure or ultimate beneficial owners include a non-resident'; those and other EEA residents pay EUR 500, others EUR 750; paid in advance, not returned on refusal. SEB's offers page (same day) sets it at EUR 0 for an Estonia-registered company 'with non-resident shareholders' until 30 November 2026; its Estonian text excludes non-EEA residents. Monthly account fee: EUR 1 (resident of Estonia), EUR 20 (EEA resident).

m-9c1cb7e7.t: Swedbank, pages read 5 October 2026: opening a business account is free (price-list section effective 1 November 2023). The account-opening page prints a 'Price list in the first year' - monthly account fee, euro payments and corporate debit card all EUR 0 - and says first-year debit cards are free 'for start-up companies'. Standing list (effective 31 August 2026): 1,000 euro payments a month free in digital channels, then EUR 0.16 intra-bank or EUR 0.38 European; Business Debit Card EUR 2 a month. 'Estonian legal persons with non-residents included as representatives or in the ownership structure' pay EUR 300 for enhanced due diligence before the decision, not returned on refusal.

m-9a7490ae.t: Luminor Bank AS's Estonian price list for business clients valid from 27.05.2022 (archive snapshot of 28 January 2023 - the newest copy reachable on 5 October 2026, the live site answering with a bot check) charged for account opening: nothing for an Estonian resident; 'per agreement, min EUR 1000' for a resident of the European Economic Area and equally for a non-resident of the EEA; EUR 500 per company for checking the data of a shareholder who is not an EU resident and holds at least 25% of a company registered in Estonia, paid before the bank decides and not refunded. An additional monthly fee of EUR 60 applied to each of these groups on top of the EUR 1 monthly account fee.

m-9a0f5e01.t: AS SEB Pank's General Terms name the e-resident's card as a ground for ending a relationship. Under clause 118.28 of the version valid as of 01.06.2026 the bank may extraordinarily cancel an agreement without advance notice if 'the state refuses to issue the Client with an e-resident's digital identity card or suspends or cancels its validity'. The ground first appears in the version valid from 01.12.2016 (clause 128.10) and is absent from the version valid from 01.06.2015. It is the only mention of e-residents in the 2026 terms: no clause deals with opening an account for an e-resident.

m-999059e8.t: For a private person who is a non-resident, Coop Pank AS's page 'Join Estonia's own bank' (read 5 October 2026) says: account opened at a branch, 'Documents reviewed for a fee of €195', and 'E-residency alone isn't a sufficient basis for opening an account for an individual: they need to have a strong link to Estonia'. The bank's private price list (section 'Settlement accounts', effective 1 August 2026) narrows the fee: inspection of documents costs EUR 195 only for a 'resident of another country (non-EEA)' and is free for an 'EEA country resident'; the non-EEA resident also pays EUR 8 a month for account maintenance. The fee is not refunded on refusal.

m-98916064.t: AS SEB Pank opens a company account remotely by video meeting only for holders of Estonian electronic identity: its page 'Open a business account remotely' (read 5 October 2026) requires the business to be registered in the Business Register, the applicant to be authorised to represent the company alone (for example a board member) and 'to have an ID-card of the Republic of Estonia, Mobile-ID or Smart-ID', and adds: 'Account opening via video meeting is available for Estonian residents.' Video meetings run on workdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. by prior registration. The e-resident's digital ID is not among the listed means.

m-971cf9ba.t: For a natural person, Swedbank AS's General Conditions effective 31 August 2026 count as a connection with Estonia 'primarily' that the person lives, studies or works in Estonia or that family members (e.g. spouse, children, parents) live there (3.3.1-3.3.2). The versions effective 01.06.2018 and 1 January 2021 also counted a right of residence in the European Union and owning property in Estonia, and those effective 1 November 2023 and 1 September 2025 still named both, in negative form. Under clause 9.2.9 of the 2026 version it is a good cause for the bank to terminate that 'the Client as a natural person does not have a right of residence in the European Union'.

m-923d3dc3.t: Swedbank AS's checklist of account-opening documents (effective 26.03.2026) states: 'Start-up accounts are opened for companies in foundation (pursuant to the Commercial Code) and for that purpose, we ask you to submit a notarized memorandum of association. Until the registration of companies, the founders/shareholders can only make payments to the start-up account.' Its business price list (section effective 01.11.2023) gives 'Opening a start-up account' as free of charge; AS SEB Pank's price list effective 01.06.2026 likewise lists 'Start-up account opening' as free of charge. The checklist does not say how a company founded online without a notary obtains a start-up account.

m-90f16502.t: The e-Residency programme describes Estonian banks' practice towards companies of non-residents (knowledge-base article updated 6 October 2025): banks 'will likely consider' either a company with 'a strong connection to Estonia' — employees in Estonia, partners and suppliers there, serving the Estonian market — or a single-shareholder company with easily traceable income; 'a personal visit to their office in Estonia is most likely required'. It also states that 'Estonian companies are not obligated to have a bank account in Estonia or use an Estonian (EE) IBAN for their business transactions', and names LHV as the Estonian bank most used by e-residents.

m-8230e889.t: AS SEB Pank's fees for a private person by residence (price list effective as of 01.06.2026, read 5 October 2026): current-account opening is free; the handling fee of documents submitted for opening is free for residents of Estonia and of EEA member states and EUR 250 for residents of another country, not returned if the bank refuses; the monthly current-account fee is EUR 0.30 for residents of Estonia and of EEA states and EUR 7 for residents of other countries (no monthly fee up to age 19 and from 65).

m-821ccbcc.t: Eesti Pank's Payments Review of March 2026 counts refused applications to open a basic payment account at all banks in Estonia: 4,237 in 2025, about 500 more than a year earlier, an estimated 3.6% of applications against 113 thousand first basic payment accounts opened. Of the 2025 refusals 2,628 concerned legal persons (2,578 resident, 50 non-resident) and 1,609 natural persons (1,099 resident, 510 non-resident). Relative to applications, non-resident legal persons were refused most often - 'nearly a third of applications'. Reasons banks gave for legal persons include a mismatch with the bank's risk appetite, an insufficient connection with Estonia and an opaque ownership structure.

m-7fe9d747.t: LHV Pank's fees for a non-resident private person (price list section 'Non-residents', valid as of 01.05.2024, read 5 October 2026): account opening application fee EUR 100 and EUR 10 a month for residents of EU member states, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland; EUR 200 and EUR 20 for residents of other countries; free for Estonian citizens and residents. The amounts match the section valid as of 01.12.2022, where the charge was called 'Account opening'. From the section valid as of 22.08.2023 it is an application fee paid before review and kept if the bank refuses; since 01.05.2024 also if the applicant cancels. Ukrainian citizens' accounts opened after 24.02.2022 are exempt.

m-7df44b8f.t: Swedbank AS's General Conditions on non-residents by version. 1 February 2016 (3.8): the bank 'shall have the right to decide at its own discretion' whether to contract with a natural or legal person not resident in Estonia. 01.06.2018 and 1 January 2021 (3.3): it contracts if the person's interests are reasonable and a connection with Estonia exists. From 1 November 2023 (kept in 2025 and 2026): it 'shall not enter into an Agreement' with a non-resident, or a person whose ownership structure or related persons include one, 'in the absence of a connection with Estonia'; since 31 August 2026 it may also require proof of 'the lawful right to live in the European Union' (3.4).

m-7cae8b19.t: LHV Pank's page for non-residents (read 5 October 2026) states for business clients: 'your company will need to prove a clear connection to Estonia and a need to open an account here'; a location-independent company registered in Estonia is asked for an overview of its activities and clients and, if possible, a business plan. It adds that 'e-resident status by itself is not a sufficient basis for opening a bank account'; that non-resident clients cannot be identified digitally and are asked to come to an LHV office, unless already identified at LHV (the agreement is then signed with the e-resident's digital ID); and that it opens no accounts for offshore-registered or offshore-owned firms.

m-7a5abb43.t: LHV Pank's General Conditions effective 09.10.2025 name what shows a 'sufficient connection with Estonia'. For a legal person: a permanent establishment in Estonia ('e.g., the person's management, employees, offices or warehouse are located in Estonia'), a need to pay wages to employees working in Estonia under an employment contract, or owning securities registered in the Estonian Central Register of Securities. For a natural person: living, studying or working in Estonia or having a legal basis for residence in the European Union, or a spouse, children or parents living in Estonia. The list is introduced by 'for example'. Registration of the company in Estonia is not among the examples.

m-79194934.t: SEB's website lists 13 editions of its Terms and conditions of current account agreement, in force from 22.05.2010, 01.11.2015, 01.12.2016, 13.01.2018, 01.01.2020, 01.01.2021, 01.01.2022, 01.12.2023, 01.01.2024, 01.01.2025, 26.06.2025, 01.06.2026 and 01.01.2027 - eleven of them taking effect between November 2015 and June 2026 (page read 5 October 2026). One term did not move in ten years: a business client must contest a payment within three months of the debit, against 13 months for a private client, in the edition of 01.12.2016 (clause 59) and in that of 01.06.2026 (clause 69) alike.

m-6ed60c51.t: LHV Pank's published position on e-residents (page 'Non-residents', read 5 October 2026): 'The e-resident's digital ID is not an identity document and e-resident status by itself is not a sufficient basis for opening a bank account'; without an Estonian passport, ID card or residence permit the applicant must submit documents proving a connection with Estonia. 'Non-resident clients can not be digitally identified': after approval the person comes to an LHV office for face-to-face identification and signing; someone already identified at LHV may sign the client agreement digitally with the e-resident's digital ID. No processing time is published - only 'we will contact you shortly'.

m-6df8ef23.t: AS SEB Pank's General Terms valid as of 01.06.2026 let the bank refuse a relationship (clause 46) or cancel it without advance notice (clause 118) on grounds tied to where the people behind a company live: the person 'has no legal basis for residing in the European Union' (46.17); 'the ultimate beneficial owner of a Business Client who is from a country with a significant risk of corruption, terrorist financing, money laundering or sanctions has no legal right to reside in the European Union' (46.19; 118.11); the person or a connected person is resident in an offshore jurisdiction or has an offshore entity in its structure or among its partners (46.13; 118.23).

m-6ce2e886.t: Coop Pank AS may end a company's account contract on one month's notice. Its Standard Terms and Conditions of Settlement Contract (applying to agreements concluded from 01.06.2026 and, from 01.08.2026, to earlier ones) give the bank 'the right to cancel the Contract entered into with a corporate client unilaterally in justified cases by notifying the client who is a legal entity about this at least one (1) month in advance' (clause 12.3.3). The two months of the bank's General Terms (clause 13.8, effective 1 October 2025) apply only 'unless otherwise set out' in the service terms. The client may cancel at any time unless other contracts require the account (12.3.1).

m-6c3759c9.t: SEB Pank's page for new business customers (read 5 October 2026) calls 'a connection to Estonia, a transparent ownership structure, and a transparent business model' the most important prerequisites for a company account; the connection can be operations strongly linked to Estonia, main partners or clients in Estonia, or goods moved through Estonia. Opening online requires, among other conditions, that the legal representative is an SEB private customer and a citizen or resident of the country with sole signing rights, and that the company, its shareholders and ultimate owners are of that country. An e-resident 'must visit a branch'. The bank 'may take up to 10 working days' to decide.

m-66bb0682.t: Coop Pank AS opens a company account online only for a narrow group: 'A business account can be opened online only if the representative is an Estonian citizen or holds a permanent residence permit in Estonia' (page read 5 October 2026); after login by Smart-ID, Mobile-ID or ID card the account opens immediately on digital signing. For a non-resident the page calls a branch 'the easiest way'; representatives who have not identified themselves at a branch must do so before signing. After electronic identification only, outgoing payments from the company account are capped at EUR 25,000 per month until identification in person. No processing time is published beyond 'as soon as possible'.

m-64fe1367.t: Swedbank AS publishes two tracks for a company account (page 'Open an account', read 5 October 2026). A representative whose identity the bank has already confirmed applies in the Internet Bank and signs with 'Smart ID, Mobile ID or an ID card': for an application made on a working day from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. 'we will contact you within an hour and you'll have a new account'. 'If the owners of the company include non-residents or foreign companies, the most convenient way to open an account is to book an appointment at the Arter branch in Tallinn', with the listed documents prepared beforehand; the bank then decides 'within 10 working days after receiving the enhanced due diligence fee'.

m-6346ebef.t: Estonian tax law does not tie tax payment to an Estonian bank account. The Tax and Customs Board's page 'Payment of taxes' (last updated 21.07.2026) has taxes paid by bank transfer, with the taxpayer's reference number, to its own accounts at SEB Pank, Swedbank, Luminor Bank, LHV Pank and Coop Pank, or in the e-MTA portal by credit card or bank link. For refunds the Taxation Act § 106 (text in force from 1 October 2026) requires only 'the taxpayer's bank account details' and expressly foresees an account abroad: when the refund is transferred 'to the taxpayer's bank account located in a foreign state' the authority may deduct the transfer costs from the refunded sum (§ 106(4)).

m-614c118a.t: A company's 'connection with Estonia' in Swedbank AS's General Conditions effective 31 August 2026 (3.3.3-3.3.4): 'primarily' that its owners are Estonian residents, or that the target market of its business is Estonia, 'including the need to pay remuneration to persons working in Estonia; the need to settle transactions with Estonian companies'. The versions in force from 2018 to 30 August 2026 were wider: business activities in Estonia, wages to persons working there, transactions with Estonian companies, or investments in Estonian property or securities. The 2026 text also lists as a good reason to refuse a person with an offshore entity in its structure or partners (3.4.10).

m-5ab3c723.t: Coop Pank AS publishes its own definition of a non-resident business (page 'Bring your business over to us', read 5 October 2026): it 'treats companies registered abroad or Estonian companies which are not controlled by an Estonian resident as non-residents'. Such an applicant must 'demonstrate that you have a clear connection to Estonia and explain what financial need will be served'. Counted as a strong connection: economic activities connected to Estonia (a permanent place of business or employees there), main partners in Estonia, a product or service aimed at the Estonian market 'e.g. an Estonian-language online store', property in Estonia or operations related to property.

m-5a29fed0.t: Coop Pank AS's price list for corporate clients (section 'Current account', effective 1 August 2026) charges for opening an account: nothing for a legal person registered in Estonia; EUR 200 if its ownership structure includes a legal person registered in, or a natural person whose identity document was issued by, another EEA state except Cyprus, Liechtenstein and Malta; EUR 500 if that link is to Cyprus, Liechtenstein, Malta or a non-EEA country and the person is not an Estonian citizen or residence-permit holder.
